Beyond their use as convergence diagnostics, these weights give unbiased estimates of the Radon-Nikodym derivative between the un-normalized target and the distribution of the current iterate, a richer object than the convergence bounds alone, with natural applications to importance-weighted inference. We show how such weightings can provide asymptotic upper bounds to any f-divergence, prove that these bounds converge to zero as the chains approach stationarity, and demonstrate that, while more conservative than existing coupling-based total variation estimators, our method remains a practical and broadly applicable diagnostic tool.

papers.title: Bayesian Transfer Operators in Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces
papers.abstract: Transfer operators provide a linear description of nonlinear dynamical systems by propagating observables or probability distributions. In reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces, these operators are represented through conditional mean embeddings, whose regularized estimator coincides with the posterior mean of Gaussian process regression. Building on this correspondence, we formulate Gaussian Process Dynamic Mode Decomposition, a Bayesian transfer-operator method that combines sparse variational Gaussian processes with kernel-based Koopman and Perron--Frobenius operator approximation. The resulting framework provides a principled route to uncertainty quantification, scalable sparse approximations, and data-adaptive dictionary learning for prediction and spectral analysis. Additionally, the model-selection formulation naturally gives rise to a forward--backward operator structure, which establishes a connection between Bayesian transfer-operator learning and time-lagged canonical correlation analysis.

papers.title: A new characterization of (pre)liminary C*-algebras
papers.abstract: We characterize separable liminary and preliminary C*-algebras by ordinal ranks and ideal filtrations. Here liminary means that every irreducible image consists of compact operators, and preliminary means that every irreducible representation is finite dimensional. The Pedersen rank stratifies the spectrum by successive local constancy of representation dimension; Fell rank minimizes the analogous local ranks arising from positive elements. We prove that a separable type I C*-algebra is liminary if and only if its Fell rank is countable. A separable C*-algebra is preliminary if and only if it has a countable continuous ideal filtration whose successive quotients are countable direct sums of homogeneous algebras of finite representation dimension. The least possible filtration length is its Pedersen length. We also determine the possible ordinal values of the two ranks. Every nonzero countable ordinal is a Pedersen rank, whereas the nonzero countable Fell ranks are exactly $ωα+1$ and $ωλ$, where $α$ is countable and $λ$ is a nonzero countable limit ordinal. All these values occur on separable preliminary approximately finite-dimensional algebras with countable Hausdorff spectra. Among nonzero separable unital algebras, the possible Pedersen ranks of preliminary algebras are exactly the countable successors, and the possible Fell ranks of liminary algebras are exactly $ωα+1$ for countable $α$.

papers.title: Limit groups with respect to Thompson's group $F$ and other hereditarily separating groups
papers.abstract: We prove that a limit group over Thompson's group $F$ cannot be an HNN-extension of $F$ with finitely generated associated subgroup. On the other hand we give an example of an $F$-limit group which is a centralized HNN-extenstions of $F$. We also study relatively limit groups with respect to $F$ and some other known groups of homeomorphisms of topological spaces. This paper revises and extends some results of the second author from arXiv:1308.6330.

papers.title: Multipole and Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless Transitions in the Two-component Plasma
papers.abstract: We study the two-dimensional two-component Coulomb gas in the canonical ensemble and at inverse temperature $β>2$. In this regime, the partition function diverges and the interaction needs to be cut off at a length scale $λ\in (0,1)$. Particles of opposite charges tend to pair into dipoles of length scale comparable to $λ$, which themselves can aggregate into multipoles. Despite the slow decay of dipole--dipole interactions, we construct a convergent cluster expansion around a hierarchical reference model that retains only intra-multipole interactions. This yields a large-deviation result for the number of $2p$-poles as well as a \textcolor{black}{free-energy expansion} as $N\to\infty$ and $λ\to0$, with three contributions: (i) the free energy of $N$ independent dipoles, (ii) a perturbative correction, and (iii) the contribution of a non-dilute subsystem. The perturbative term has two equivalent characterizations: (a) a convergent Mayer series built from non-divergent elementary dipole activities; and (b) a variational formula as the minimum of a large-deviation rate function for the empirical counts of $2p$-poles. The Mayer coefficients \textcolor{black}{should undergo} transitions at $β_p=4-\tfrac{2}{p}$\textcolor{black}{, and these thresholds} accumulate at $β=4$, which corresponds to the \textcolor{black}{Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless} transition in the low-dipole-density limit. \textcolor{black}{We prove that the limiting $p$-dipole activities are finite for $β>β_p$.} The non-dilute system corresponds to the contribution of large dipoles. For $2<β<4$, the independent-dipole dilution estimate predicts the critical length scale $R_{β,λ}=λ^{-(β-2)/(4-β)}$. For $β\geq4$, we set $R_{β,λ}=+\infty$, as this estimate gives no algebraic crossover scale in $λ$.

papers.title: Toric geometry of ReLU neural networks
papers.abstract: Given a continuous piecewise linear function $f:\mathbb{R}^{n_0} \to \mathbb{R}$ and a fixed architecture of feedforward ReLU neural networks, the exact function realization problem asks when a network of that architecture realizes $f$. In contrast, expressivity concerns characterizing all functions exactly realizable by a given architecture. To address these questions systematically, we establish a connection between toric geometry and ReLU neural networks, allowing tools from algebraic geometry to analyze the structures. Starting with an unbiased ReLU network with rational weights, we define the ReLU fan, the ReLU toric variety, and the ReLU Cartier divisor associated with the network. This work also relates the tropical and the toric geometry: the former captures combinatorial data of ReLU networks, while the latter recovers the underlying geometric structure. As an application, we obtain a complete characterization of the functions realizable by unbiased shallow ReLU networks with rational weights. The characterization is expressed in terms of intersection numbers of ReLU Cartier divisors with torus-invariant curves and leads to a decomposition of piecewise-linear functions into shallow and non-shallow components.

papers.title: Multi-period Asset-liability Management with Reinforcement Learning in a Regime-Switching Market
papers.abstract: This paper explores the mean-variance portfolio selection problem in a multi-period financial market characterized by regime-switching dynamics and uncontrollable liabilities. To address the uncertainty in the decision-making process within the financial market, we incorporate reinforcement learning (RL) techniques. Specifically, the study examines an exploratory mean-variance (EMV) framework where investors aim to minimize risk while maximizing returns under incomplete market information, influenced by shifting economic regimes. The market model includes risk-free and risky assets, with liability dynamics driven by a Markov regime-switching process. To align with real-world scenarios where financial decisions are made over discrete time periods, we adopt a multi-period dynamic model. We present an optimal portfolio strategy derived using RL techniques that adapt to these market conditions. The proposed solution addresses the inherent time inconsistency in classical mean-variance models by integrating a pre-committed strategy formulation. Furthermore, we incorporate partial market observability, employing stochastic filtering techniques to estimate unobservable market states. Numerical simulations and empirical tests on real financial data demonstrate that our method achieves superior returns, lower risk, and faster convergence compared to traditional models. These findings highlight the robustness and adaptability of our RL-based solution in dynamic and complex financial environments.

papers.title: On the Parameterized Complexity of Grundy Domination and Zero Forcing Problems
papers.abstract: We consider two different problem families that deal with domination in graphs. On the one hand, we focus on dominating sequences. In such a sequence, every vertex dominates some vertex of the graph that was not dominated by any earlier vertex in the sequence. The problem of finding the longest dominating sequence is known as $\mathsf{Grundy~Domination}$. Depending on whether the closed or the open neighborhoods are used for domination, there are three other versions of this problem: $\mathsf{Grundy~Total~Domination}$, $\mathsf{L\text{-}Grundy~Domination}$, and $\mathsf{Z\text{-}Grundy~Domination}$. We show that all four problem variants are $\mathsf{W[1]}$-complete when parameterized by the solution size. On the other hand, we consider the family of zero forcing problems which form the parametric duals of the Grundy domination problems. In these problems, one looks for the smallest set of vertices initially colored blue such that certain color change rules are able to color all other vertices blue. It has been shown that the dual of $\mathsf{Z\text{-}Grundy~Domination}$, known as $\mathsf{Zero~Forcing~Set}$, is in $\mathsf{FPT}$ when parameterized by the treewidth or the solution size. We extend the treewidth result to the other three variants of zero forcing and their respective Grundy domination problems. Our algorithm also implies an $\mathsf{FPT}$ algorithm for $\mathsf{Grundy~Domination}$ when parameterized by the number of vertices that are not in the dominating sequence. In contrast, we show that $\mathsf{L\text{-}Grundy~Domination}$ is $\mathsf{W[1]}$-hard for that parameter.

papers.title: A generalized Hurwitz stability criterion via rectangular block Hankel matrices for nonmonic matrix polynomials
papers.abstract: We develop a Hurwitz stability criterion for nonmonic matrix polynomials via column reduction, generalizing existing approaches constrained by the monic assumption and thus serving as a more natural extension of Gantmacher's classical stability criterion via Markov parameters. Starting from redefining the associated Markov parameters through an adaptive column-wise Lienard-Chipart splitting method, our framework constructs two structured matrices whose rectangular Hankel blocks are obtained via the extraction of these parameters. We establish an explicit interrelation between the inertia of column reduced matrix polynomials and the derived structured matrices. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the Hurwitz stability of column reduced matrix polynomials can be determined by the Hermitian positive definiteness of these rectangular block Hankel matrices.

papers.title: Medians, Oscillations, and Distance Functions
papers.abstract: Vasin (for $n=1$) and Anderson, Lehrbäck, Mudarra, and Vähäkangas (arXiv:2209.06284) (for $n>1$) provided a geometric characterization of the sets $E \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ for which $w = \operatorname{dist}(\cdot, E)^{-α}$ is a Muckenhoupt $A_1$ weight for some $α> 0$. In this paper, we provide a geometric characterization of the sets $E \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ (which we call median porous sets) such that $w = \operatorname{dist}(\cdot, E)^{-α}$ is a Muckenhoupt $A_p$ weight for some $α> 0$ (given any $1 < p \leq \infty$). Given $1 < p \leq \infty$, we also find the precise range of exponents $α$ for which $w = \operatorname{dist}(\cdot, E)^{-α} \in A_p$, in analogy to the $p=1$ case done in arXiv:2209.06284. With our characterization, we prove that $\mathbb{R}^n \setminus E$ supports a Hardy-Sobolev inequality if $E$ is an appropriate median porous set. The proofs rely on a new median-value characterization of $BMO$: For a real-valued measurable function on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and constants $0 < s < t < 1$, \[\|f\|_{BMO} \approx_{s, t, n} \sup_{Q}[M_t(f, Q) - M_s(f, Q)]\] where $M_s(f, Q)$ denotes the $s$-median value of $f$ on $Q$.

papers.title: Recovering the Euclidean Geometry of High-Dimensional Data Under Heterogeneous Noise
papers.abstract: Pairwise Euclidean distances provide a simple geometric representation of high-dimensional data and underlie many data analysis methods, including clustering, visualization, and manifold learning. However, in real-world applications, these distances can be severely corrupted by heterogeneous noise, where different data points are subject to different, and potentially large, noise levels. Such noise distorts the distances inhomogeneously, leading to a misrepresentation of the underlying data geometry. In this work, we ask whether the underlying clean Euclidean geometry can nevertheless be recovered from the corrupted pairwise distances. We answer this question affirmatively, showing that, perhaps surprisingly, such recovery is possible across a broad class of high-dimensional settings with underlying low-dimensional geometry, even when the noise magnitudes vary substantially across observations. We develop a principled approach for recovering the clean pairwise distances, without prior knowledge of either the clean data structure or the noise distribution, and establish probabilistic recovery guarantees. In particular, the recovery error converges to zero at polynomial rates as the feature dimension and dataset size increase simultaneously. Experiments on synthetic datasets demonstrate accurate recovery of the Euclidean geometry in challenging regimes and improved robustness of downstream methods that rely on pairwise distances. When applied to real single-cell RNA sequencing data, our method reliably recovers local neighborhood structure, enabling accurate nearest-neighbor identification used in many downstream analyses.

papers.title: Semiadditive Alternating Powers and Twisted Power Operations
papers.abstract: We study a class of representations of symmetric groups in higher semiadditive categories. For these representations in $\mathrm{Mod}^{\wedge}_{E_n}$, the transchromatic character of Hopkins--Kuhn--Ravenel and Stapleton is recovered as a sequence of monoidal characters on suitable categorifications, giving an explicit algorithm for its computation, and relating it to the iterated monoidal character in $(\infty,n)$-categories. These representations also give rise to notions of alternating powers and power operations in semiadditive categories, extending the classical alternating powers and $λ$-operations in $\mathrm{K}$-theory. We provide explicit computations in both the chromatic and higher categorical settings at low heights.

papers.title: Two Tiling is Undecidable
papers.abstract: We show that the following problem is undecidable: given two polygonal prototiles, determine whether the plane can be tiled with rotated and translated copies of them. This improves a result of Demaine and Langerman [SoCG 2025], who showed undecidability for three tiles. Along the way, we show that tiling with one prototile is undecidable if there can be edge-to-edge matching rules. This is the first result to show undecidability for monotiling with only local matching constraints.

papers.title: Ideals generated by corner-interval minors
papers.abstract: In this article, we study binomial ideals generated by an arbitrary collection of corner-interval $2$-minors of a generic matrix. We determine the minimal prime ideals of such ideals and characterize their radicality in the special case of corner minors. Moreover, we discuss connectivity properties of contingency tables in algebraic statistics. We compute the Hilbert-Poincaré polynomial of the ideal generated by the set of all corner-interval minors and we derive the formula for the regularity in the case of corner minors.

papers.title: Automorphism groups of solvable groups of finite abelian ranks
papers.abstract: This paper gives a new explicit construction of the $\mathbb{Q}$-algebraic hull for virtually solvable groups $Γ$ of finite abelian ranks, taking into account the spectrum $S$ of the group $Γ$. As an application, we make a detailed study of the structure of $Aut(Γ)$ in the finitely generated case and show that a number of natural subgroups are $S$-arithmetic under the condition that $Fitt(Γ)$ is $S$-arithmetic. We then proceed by demonstrating that $Out(Γ)$ has a $S$-arithmetic image in the group of algebraic outer automorphisms of the $\mathbb{Q}$-algebraic hull. We finish by discussing further applications of the $\mathbb{Q}$-algebraic hull towards an open conjecture by Nekrashevych and Pete and topological fixed point theory.

papers.title: Entropic smoothing and gradient approximation for Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization
papers.abstract: Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization offers a framework for model fitting in machine learning under potential shifts in the data distribution. We study a regularized variant of this problem in which entropic smoothing produces a sampled approximation of the original objective. We establish convergence of the approximate gradients to subgradients of the unregularized objective as the regularization parameter vanishes, enabling convergence guarantees for stochastic gradient methods. We obtain qualitative convergence results under general assumptions and provide convergence rates under additional regularity. In particular, we prove rates for the convergence of the unregularized objective values, up to sampling errors, when the regularization level is decreased across iterations. Our analysis also yields results of independent interest on approximating the subdifferentials of maximum functions by gradients of their smooth approximations, together with growth-based lower bounds on optimal dual variables in Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization.

papers.title: Bias-Optimal Bounds for Stochastic Gradient Descent
papers.abstract: The non-asymptotic analysis of Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) typically yields bounds that decompose into a bias term and a variance term. In this work, we focus on the bias component and study the extent to which SGD can match the optimal convergence behavior of deterministic gradient descent. Assuming only (strong) convexity and smoothness of the objective, we derive new bounds for the full range of constant step-sizes $γL \in (0,2)$. This includes critical and large step-size regimes that were previously unexplored without additional variance assumptions, in both the convex and strongly convex cases. Those bounds are bias-optimal, in the sense that the bias term coincides with the worst-case rate of gradient descent, for all non-critical step-sizes. For critical step-sizes, we show that no bounds can be obtained with an optimal bias term, but that this optimal bias can be approximated arbitrarily closely. As an immediate application, we provide new complexity bounds for the Stochastic Proximal algorithm, without the need of regularity assumptions.

papers.title: Evaluating the Generalizability and Explainability of Firn Image Classification with Topological Features
papers.abstract: In this paper we evaluate the performance of topological features for generalizable and explainable classification of firn image data, with the broader goal of understanding the advantages, pitfalls, and trade-offs in topological featurization. Firn refers to layers of granular snow within glaciers that haven't yet been compressed into ice. This compaction process imposes distinct topological and geometric structure on firn that varies with depth within the firn column. However, the limited and highly correlated training data available results in naive classifiers (such as convolutional neural networks) overfitting to orientation-dependent features. This motivates us to evaluate topological data analysis (TDA) as a way to design features which capture the shape of the firn data while retaining a large degree of invariance. We evaluate two classes of topological features, sublevel set features and distance transform features, together with persistence curves, to predict sample depth from firn images. A range of challenging training-test scenarios reveals that no one choice of method dominates in all categories. In particular, we see a tradeoff between accuracy on the one hand, and generalizability and explainability (via feature importance) on the other.

papers.title: A definition of the background state of the atmosphere using optimal transport
papers.abstract: The dynamics of atmospheric disturbances are often described in terms of displacements of air parcels relative to their locations in a notional background state. Modified Lagrangian Mean (MLM) states have been proposed by M. E. McIntyre using the Lagrangian conserved variables potential vorticity and potential temperature to label air masses in the instantaneous 3-D atmospheric state, and then rearranging air masses sandwiched between potential vorticity contours in potential temperature layers so that they are zonally symmetric. Methven and Berrisford used conservation of Kelvin's circulation to define the distribution of MLM state mass in zonal angular momentum ($z$) and potential temperature ($θ$) coordinates given 3-D global data. We prove that for any such mass distribution in $(z, θ)$ there exists a mapping to a unique mass distribution in geophysical coordinates (latitude and pressure) which minimises energy and completely defines the MLM state in a single hemisphere. Since the state is an energy minimum, it is suitable for quantification of finite amplitude disturbances and examining atmospheric instability. This state is obtained by solving a free surface problem, which we frame as the minimisation of an optimal transport cost over a class of source measures. The solution consists of a source measure, encoding surface pressure, and an optimal transport map, connecting the distribution of mass in geophysical coordinates to the known distribution of mass in $(z, θ)$. We show that this problem reduces to an optimal transport problem with a known source measure, which has a numerically feasible discretisation, and we present a numerical solution using atmospheric reanalysis data. Additionally, our results hold for a large class of cost functions, and generalise analogous results on free surface variants of the semi-geostrophic equations.

papers.title: Triadic structures in multislice networks
papers.abstract: Networks provide a popular representation of complex data. Often, different types of relational measurements are taken on the same subjects. Such data can be represented as a multislice network, a collection of networks on the same set of nodes, with connections between nodes of different layers. For the analysis of multislice networks, we take inspiration from the analysis of simple networks, for which small subgraphs (motifs) have proven to be useful; motifs are even seen as building blocks of complex networks. A particular instance of a motif is a triangle, and while triangle counts are well understood for simple network models such as Erdős-Rényi random graphs, with i.i.d. distributed edges, even for simple multislice network models little is known about triangle counts. Here we address this issue by extending the analysis of triadic structures to multislice Erdős-Rényi networks. Again taking inspiration from the analysis of sparse Erdős-Rényi random graphs, we show that the distribution of triangles across multiple layers in a multislice Erdős-Rényi network can be well approximated by an appropriate Poisson distribution. This theoretical result opens the door to statistical goodness of fit tests for multislice networks.

papers.title: Exact module categories over $\mathrm{Rep}(u_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2))$
papers.abstract: We give a complete list of indecomposable exact module categories over the finite tensor category $\mathrm{Rep}(u_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2))$ of representations of the small quantum group $u_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$, where $q$ is a root of unity of odd order. Each of them is given as the category of representations of a left comodule algebra over $u_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ explicitly presented by generators and relations.

papers.title: Skein and cluster algebras of punctured surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove the full Fock--Goncharov conjecture for the $\mathcal{A}_{SL_2,Σ_{g,p}}$-cluster variety associated with the moduli space of decorated twisted $SL_2$-local systems on triangulable surfaces $Σ_{g,p}$ with at least two punctures. Equivalently, we show that the tagged skein algebra $Sk^{ta}(Σ)$, identified with the middle cluster algebra $\mathrm{mid}(\mathcal{A})$, coincides with the upper cluster algebra $U(Σ)$. We also introduce a localized cluster variety $\mathring{\mathcal{A}}$ whose positive real locus is the decorated Teichmüller space $\mathcal{T}^d(Σ)$. For $p\geq2$, its ring of global sections is the normalization of the classical Roger--Yang skein algebra $Sk^{RY}_{q\to1}(Σ)$ and equals that algebra except for the four-punctured sphere. In the equality cases, the quantum Roger--Yang skein algebra $Sk^{RY}_q(Σ)$ provides a quantization of this global-section ring. We prove normality of $Sk^{ta}(Σ)$ for $p\geq2$, complementing its known Gorenstein property, and normality of $Sk^{RY}_{q\to1}(Σ)$ for every triangulable $Σ_{g,p}$ other than $Σ_{0,4}$. We also prove finite generation of $U(Σ_{g,p})$ for every triangulable $Σ_{g,p}$, including the once-punctured case.

papers.title: Rubik's Abstract Polytopes
papers.abstract: We generalize the Rubik's cube, together with its group of configurations, to any abstract regular polytope. We discuss general aspects, and provide a description of the group of the Rubik's simplex in arbitrary dimension, and of Rubik's tori. We sketch an analogous argument for the Rubik's hypercube as well.

papers.title: Positivity of line bundles on general blow ups of Hirzebruch surfaces
papers.abstract: We investigate various positivity properties of line bundles on general blow ups of Hirzebruch surfaces motivated by \cite{Han}, where the author has studied general blow ups of $\mathbb{P}^2$. For each of the properties: ampleness, global generation, very ampleness, and $k$-very ampleness, we provide several sufficient numerical conditions.

papers.title: Extensibility and denseness of periodic monoid actions
papers.abstract: A monoid has the periodic approximation (PA) property if, for every full shift on a finite alphabet, finitely supported invariant probability measures are weak-* dense in the space of invariant Borel probability measures. We introduce the class of measure-theoretically extension-compatible (MEC) monoids, consisting of embeddable monoids for which every probability measure-preserving (p.m.p.) action admits an invertible p.m.p. extension. For an embeddable monoid $S$ with free $S$-group $(Γ,γ)$, we prove that the PA property implies MEC, and that the converse holds whenever $Γ$ has the PA property. We establish that every left reversible bicancellative monoid and every finitely generated free monoid is MEC, and deduce the PA property for left amenable monoids that are residually a finite group and for finitely generated free monoids. Moreover, for $S=\mathbb F_d^+$, we characterize the free $S$-group as the unique receiving $S$-group for which all fully supported invariant Markov measures on full shifts on finite alphabets admit invariant invertible extensions.

papers.title: Branching Ratios of Input Trees for Directed Multigraphs
papers.abstract: We define the branching ratio of the input tree of a node in a finite directed multigraph, prove that it exists for every node, and show that it is equal to the largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix of the induced subgraph determined by all upstream nodes. This real eigenvalue exists by the Perron-Frobenius Theorem for non-negative matrices. We motivate our analysis with simple examples, obtain information about the asymptotics for the limit growth of the input tree, and establish other basic properties of the branching ratio.

papers.title: Dimension-free Fourier restriction inequalities
papers.abstract: Let ${{\bf R}_{\mathbb{S}^{d-1}}}(p\to q)$ denote the best constant for the $L^p(\mathbb{R}^d)\to L^q(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})$ Fourier restriction inequality to the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$, and let ${\bf R}_{\mathbb{S}^{d-1}} (p\to q;\textrm{rad})$ denote the corresponding constant for radial functions. We investigate the asymptotic behavior of the operator norms ${{\bf R}_{\mathbb{S}^{d-1}}}(p\to q)$ and ${\bf R}_{\mathbb{S}^{d-1}} (p\to q;\textrm{rad})$ as the dimension $d$ tends to infinity. We further establish a dimension-free endpoint Stein-Tomas inequality for radial functions, together with the corresponding estimate for general functions which we prove with an $O(d^{1/2})$ dependence. Our methods rely on a uniform two-sided refinement of Stempak's asymptotic $L^p$ estimate of Bessel functions.

papers.title: Triangulations of the 3-sphere with knotted edge
papers.abstract: We prove that for any knot $K$, there exists a one-vertex triangulation of the $3$-sphere containing an edge forming $K$. The proof is constructive, and based on fully augmented links. We use our method to produce ``complicated'' simplicial triangulations of the $3$-sphere that we show are smallest possible, up to a constant multiplicative factor.

papers.title: On reality of eigenvalues of banded block Toeplitz matrices
papers.abstract: We formulate and partially prove a general conjecture providing necessary and sufficient conditions for the reality of the asymptotic spectrum of an arbitrary real banded block Toeplitz matrix. Additionally we present numerical experiments supporting it. This conjecture is a direct generalization of the already existing one in the case of banded Toeplitz matrices.

papers.title: Stabilities of the Kleitman diameter theorem
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a family of subsets of $[n]$. The diameter of $\mathcal{F}$ is defined as the maximum size of the symmetric difference between any two of its members. Resolving a conjecture of Erdős, Kleitman determined the maximum size of a family with fixed diameter. Specifically, if $2\leq s\leq n-2$ and $\mathcal{F}\subseteq2^{[n]}$ is a family with diameter $s$, then for $s=2d$, $|\mathcal{F}|\le \sum_{i=0}^d {n \choose i}$; for $s=2d+1$, $|\mathcal{F}|\le \sum_{i=0}^d {n \choose i} + {n-1 \choose d}$. This result, known as the Kleitman diameter theorem, generalizes both the Katona union theorem and the Erdős--Ko--Rado theorem. In 2017, Frankl provided a complete characterization of the extremal families for Kleitman's theorem and established a stability result. In this paper, we determine the extremal families for Frankl's theorem and prove a further stability result of Kleitman's theorem. This solves a recent problem proposed by Li and Wu and provides the second stability for the Kleitman diameter theorem.

papers.title: Quandle Cohomology Quiver Representations
papers.abstract: We define a family of quiver representation-valued invariants of oriented classical and virtual knots and links associated to a choice of finite quandle $X$, abelian group $A$, set of quandle 2-cocycles $C\subset H^2_Q(x;A)$, choice of coefficient ring $k$ and set of quandle endomorphisms $S\subset \mathrm{Hom}(X,X)$. From this representation we define four new polynomial (or ``polynomial'' depending on $A$) invariants. We generalize to the case of biquandles and compute some examples.

papers.title: Tilted Solid-On-Solid is liquid: scaling limit of SOS with a potential on a slope
papers.abstract:
The $(2+1)$D Solid-On-Solid (SOS) model famously exhibits a roughening transition: on an $N	imes N$ torus with the height at the origin rooted at $0$, the variance of $h(x)$, the height at $x$, is $O(1)$ at large inverse-temperature $β$, vs $\asymp \log |x|$ at small $β$ (as in the Gaussian free field (GFF)). The former--rigidity at large $β$--is known for a wide class of $|
ablaφ|^p$ models ($p=1$ being SOS) yet is believed to fail once the surface is on a slope (tilted boundary conditions). It is conjectured that the slope would destabilize the rigidity and induce the GFF-type behavior of the surface at small $β$. The only rigorous result on this is by Sheffield '05: for these models of integer height functions, if the slope $θ$ is irrational, then Var$(h(x))	o\infty$ with $|x|$ (with no known quantitative bound). We study a family of SOS surfaces at a large enough fixed $β$, on an $N	imes N$ torus with a nonzero boundary condition slope $θ$, perturbed by a potential $V$ on an $ε_β$-fraction of sites (arbitrarily small). Our main result is (a) the measure on the height gradients $
abla h$ has a limit $μ_\infty$ as $N	o\infty$; and (b) the scaling limit of a sample from $μ_\infty$ converges to a full plane GFF. In particular, we recover the asymptotics Var$(h(x))\sim c\log|x|$. To our knowledge, this is the first example of a tilted $|
ablaφ|^p$ model, or a perturbation thereof, where the limit is recovered at large $β$. The proof looks at random monotone surfaces that approximate the SOS surface, and shows that (i) these form a weakly interacting dimer model, and (ii) the renormalization framework of Giuliani, Mastropietro and Toninelli '17 leads to the GFF limit. New ingredients are needed in both parts, including a nontrivial extension of [GMT17] from finite interactions to ones with exponential decay in the radius.

papers.title: Positivity, cross-ratios, photons, and the Collar Lemma
papers.abstract: We prove that $Θ$-positive representations of fundamental groups of surfaces (possibly cusped or of infinite type) satisfy a collar lemma, and their associated cross-ratios are positive. As a consequence we deduce that $Θ$-positive representations form closed subsets of the representation variety. Along the way we systematically study a class of curves inside general flag manifolds that we call photons. Using their interplay with transversality in the flag manifold, we construct photon projections, which we use to relate the cross-ratios on the photons to the cross-ratios on the flag manifolds.

papers.title: On Sparsity and Sub-Gaussianity in the Johnson-Lindenstrauss Lemma
papers.abstract: We provide a simple proof of the Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma for sub-Gaussian variables. We extend the analysis to identify how sparse projections can be, and what the cost of sparsity is on the target dimension. The Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma is the theoretical core of the dimensionality reduction methods based on random projections. While its original formulation involves matrices with Gaussian entries, the computational cost of random projections can be drastically reduced by the use of simpler variables, especially if they vanish with a high probability. In this paper, we propose a simple and elementary analysis of random projections under classical assumptions that emphasizes the key role of sub-Gaussianity. Furthermore, we show how to extend it to sparse projections, emphasizing the limits induced by the sparsity of the data itself.

papers.title: The Column-Diamond Resolution over Quadratic Monomial Rings
papers.abstract: We study infinite minimal free resolutions of modules $M = R/(x_{i_1},\ldots,x_{i_m})$ over quadratic monomial rings $R = k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/I$. We introduce the Column-Diamond construction, a recursive diagrammatic procedure that builds an explicit free resolution of $M$ from columns and diamonds determined by the quadratic generators of $I$. We prove that this resolution is exact and minimal. As an application, the Betti numbers of $M$ are counted by valid words in a graph associated to $I$, which yields a combinatorial rational formula for the Poincaré series.

papers.title: Fluctuations in the non-linear supersymmetric hyperbolic sigma model with hierarchical interactions
papers.abstract: We consider a class of non-linear supersymmetric hyperbolic sigma models on a hierarchical lattice. We prove that the hyperbolic distance between the superspin at any vertex and a reference superspin has asymptotically small fluctuations for large enough interactions, uniformly in the size of the graph and in the choice of the vertex. This can be viewed as a spontaneous breaking of the Lorentz boost symmetry.

papers.title: Degenerations of nilalgebras
papers.abstract: All complex $3$-dimensional nilalgebras were described. As a corollary, all degenerations in the variety of complex $3$-dimensional nilalgebras were obtained.

papers.title: Random Abstract Cell Complexes
papers.abstract: In machine learning and signal processing, methods based on (abstract) cell complexes (CCs) are being applied successfully in different applications. However, there is currently a lack of random models, which are necessary for a thorough evaluation of these methods, both by generating synthetic data and as null models to compare results to. We fill this gap by defining a random model for abstract cell complexes based on independent inclusion probabilities, similar to the Erdős-Rényi model for graphs. We also discuss how modifications to bias the model to incorporate more structure can be implemented. The model can also be used to lift a graph (or other cell complex) to a cell complex of arbitrary dimension. The main challenge in this is that the number of cycles (possible 2-cells) on graphs is exponential, and the same is true in higher dimensions. We overcome this complexity with an approximate sampling algorithm limited to 2-cells (polygons) that is based on a recent advance in sampling cycles on a graph. Using this algorithm, we analyze the properties of random 2-dimensional CCs and showcase its usage as a performance baseline for both topological signal processing and topological deep learning. The algorithm is available in the package py-raccoon on the Python Package Index.

papers.title: A calculus of scalar maximally monotone operators for aggregation and tail control
papers.abstract: We give simple criteria for sums, nonnegative products and compositions of scalar maximally monotone operators to preserve maximality, and introduce a pointwise resolvent order with associated infima and suprema. We first apply this framework to the Hardy transform to derive sharp bounds for nonlinear aggregation in terms of marginal upper-tail means, without independence assumptions. We then employ a geometric version of the Hardy transform (the geometric mean operator) to establish concentration inequalities for nonlinear observations with multiplicative random Lipschitz controls. No exponential tail decay is required, and the result covers heavy-tailed settings under logarithmic integrability assumptions. Feed-forward neural networks illustrate the latter result.

papers.title: Traveling waves of NLS system arising in optical material without Galilean symmetry
papers.abstract: We study a nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) system with cubic interactions arising in nonlinear optics, focusing on how the absence of Galilean symmetry affects solution dynamics. In the mass-critical case, we establish a new global existence result that contrasts with classical results. By exploiting the properties of traveling solitary waves, we obtain a condition on the initial data that relaxes the standard sharp assumptions. We also characterize the high-frequency limit of these traveling solitary waves as the frequency $ω$ tends to infinity.

papers.title: De Rham logarithmic classes and Tate conjecture
papers.abstract: We introduce the definition of De Rham logarithmic classes. We show that the De Rham class of an algebraic cycle of a smooth algebraic variety over a field of characteristic zero is logarithmic and conversely that a logarithmic class of bidegree $(d,d)$ is the De Rham class of an algebraic cycle (of codimension $d$). We also give for smooth algebraic varieties over a $p$-adic field an analytic version of this result. We deduce from the analytic case the Tate conjecture for smooth projective varieties over fields of finite type over $\mathbb Q$.

papers.title: Online Nonconvex Decision Making with Approximate Oracles
papers.abstract: We study online decision making with possibly nonconvex (for example, combinatorial or integer) local feasible sets and convex long-term constraints. At each period, a decision maker selects a local action to maximize cumulative reward while ensuring that the sequence of actions satisfies the global constraints in the long term. It is known that $O(\sqrt{T})$ long-term constraint violation and $O(\sqrt{T})$ reward regret are achievable if given access to a local optimization oracle that exactly solves optimization problems over each local feasible set. Instead of requiring exact optimization over each local feasible set, we assume access to an approximate local optimization oracle that permits optimization errors quantified by two parameters $(δ_+,δ_\times)$. We develop an approximate online dual mirror descent algorithm and show that its guarantees depend on a feasibility slack parameter $\underline d$, which measures the compatibility between local feasible sets and the long-term constraint. Under the standard random permutation model, when $δ_+=O(1)$, $δ_\times<\underline d$ and $\underline d-δ_\times=Ω(1)$, the algorithm achieves $O(\sqrt T)$ long-term constraint violation and reward regret up to $O\bigl(\sqrt T+δ_\times T\bigr)+δ_+ T$. We also show a matching limitation: when $δ_+=0$ and $δ_\times>\underline d$, no online algorithm relying on such approximate oracle outputs can guarantee sublinear long-term constraint violation in general.

papers.title: Demystifying the characterization of SDP matrices in mathematical programming
papers.abstract: This manuscript was written because I found no other introduction to SDP programming that targets the same audience. A first difference compared to other existing introductions to SDP is that this work comes out of a mind that was itself struggling to understand. This may seem to be only a weakness, but, paradoxically, it is both a weakness and a strength. First, I did not try to overpower the reader, but I tried to minimize the distance between the author and the reader as much as possible, even hoping to achieve a small level of mutual empathy. This enabled me avoid a quite common pitfall: many long-acknowledged experts tend to forget the difficulties of beginners. Other experts try to make all proofs as short as possible and to dismiss as unimportant certain key results they have seen thousands of time in their career. I also avoided this, even if I did shorten a few proofs when I revised this manuscript two years after it was first written. However, I also kept certain proofs that seem longer than necessary because I feel they offer more insight; an important goal is to capture the "spirit" of each proven result instead of reducing it to a flow of formulae. The very first key step towards mastering SDP programming is to get full insight into the eigen-decomposition of real symmetric matrices. It is enough to see the way many other introductions to SDP programming address this eigen-decomposition to understand that their target audience is different from mine. They often list the eigen-decomposition without proof, while I give two proofs to really familiarize the reader with it.

papers.title: The extremal process of a cascading family of branching Brownian motion
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic behaviour of the extremal process of a cascading family of branching Brownian motions. This is a particle system on the real line such that each particle has a type in addition to his position. Particles of type $1$ move on the real line according to Brownian motions and branch at rate $1$ into two children of type $1$. Furthermore, at rate $α$, they give birth to children too of type $2$. Particles of type $2$ move according to standard Brownian motion and branch at rate $1$, but cannot give birth to descendants of type $1$. We obtain the asymptotic behaviour of the extremal process of particles of type $2$.

papers.title: Minimal Systems of Binomial Generators for the Ideals of Certain Monomial Curves
papers.abstract: Let $a, b$ and $n > 1$ be three positive integers such that $a$ and $\sum_{j=0}^{n-1} b^j$ are relatively prime. In this paper, we prove that the toric ideal $I$ associated to the submonoid of $\mathbb{N}$ generated by $\{\sum_{j=0}^{n-1} b^j\} \cup \{\sum_{j=0}^{n-1} b^j + a\, \sum_{j=0}^{i-2} b^j \mid i = 2, \ldots, n\}$ is determinantal. Moreover, we prove that for $n > 3$, the ideal $I$ has a unique minimal system of generators if and only if $a < b-1$.

papers.title: Two-term silting and $τ$-cluster morphism categories
papers.abstract: We generalise $τ$-cluster morphism categories to the setting of non-positive dg algebras with finite dimensional cohomology in all degrees. The compatibility of silting reduction with support $τ$-tilting reduction will be an essential ingredient when linking our definition to those of Buan--Marsh and Buan--Hanson.

papers.title: Rational Solutions of Abel Differential Equations
papers.abstract: We study the rational solutions of the Abel equation $x'=A(t)x^3+B(t)x^2$ where $A$ and $B \in \mathbb{C}[t]$. We prove that if $°(A)$ is even or $°(B)>(°(A)-1)/2$ then the equation has at most two rational solutions. For any other case, an upper bound on the number of rational solutions is obtained. Moreover, we prove that if there are more than $(°(A)+1)/2$ rational solutions then the equation admits a Darboux first integral.

papers.title: Cohomology and Deformation of Leibniz Superalgebras
papers.abstract: In this article, we give a characterization of Leibniz superalgebras. We study cohomology theory of Leibniz superalgebras. Using the cohomology we study the formal deformation theory of Leibniz superalgebras. We do some cohomology computation in lower dimensions. We establish a one to one correspondence between extensions of a Leibniz superalgebra and its cohomology group in dimension 2.

papers.title: A Note on Decomposable and Reducible Integer Matrices
papers.abstract: We propose necessary and sufficient conditions for an integer matrix to be decomposable in terms of its Hermite normal form. Specifically, to each integer matrix, we associate a symmetric integer matrix whose reducibility can be efficiently determined by elementary linear algebra techniques, and which completely determines the decomposability of the first one.

papers.title: Holomorphic vector fields and rationality
papers.abstract: We prove Carrell's conjecture that a smooth complex projective variety with a holomorphic vector field having a nonempty finite zero set is rational. The proof uses slices for projective additive group actions and a birational invariant in the dimension-graded Grothendieck ring. For a vector field with one zero, we bound the second Betti number by the dimension of the kernel of the linear part at that zero. A multiplicative group that normalizes the additive action with a nontrivial character gives a product formula for the Betti numbers and a sharp upper bound for the Euler characteristic. We classify smooth projective surfaces admitting a holomorphic vector field with exactly one zero. Among smooth projective threefolds of Picard number one admitting a holomorphic vector field with exactly one zero, there are five isomorphism types.

papers.title: The algebraic and geometric classification of nilpotent binary Lie algebras
papers.abstract: The paper is devoted to give the complete algebraic classification of nilpotent binary Lie algebras of dimension $\leq 6$ over an arbitrary base field ${\mathbb{F}}$ of characteristic not $2$ and the complete geometric classification of nilpotent binary Lie algebras of dimension $6$ over $\mathbb C.$ As an application, we have the algebraic and geometric classification of nilpotent anticommutative $\mathfrak{CD}$-algebras of dimension $\leq 6.$

papers.title: Time Relaxation with Iterative Modified Lavrentiev Regularization
papers.abstract: We study a time relaxation regularization of the Navier--Stokes equations, \[u_t+u\cdot\nabla u+\nabla p-νΔu+\tfracχδ(u-D_N\bar u)=f,\] in which $\bar u$ is the differential filter of radius $δ$ applied to $u$ and $D_N$ is the iterated modified Lavrentiev deconvolution operator with regularization parameter $α$. We first show that the relaxation term has a simple closed form: it is a filtered hyperviscosity, $ν_N(-Δ)^{N+1}G_{\sqrtαδ}^{N+1}u$ with $ν_N=χα^{N+1}δ^{2N+1}$, where $G_{\sqrtαδ}$ is the differential filter of the smaller radius $\sqrtα\,δ$. From this we obtain sharp consistency bounds, the existence of weak solutions with an energy inequality, and an explicit estimate showing that the energy in scales below any given length is $O(δ/χ)$ as $χ\to\infty$. Extending a result of Pakzad for van Cittert deconvolution, we bound the time-averaged energy dissipation rate by $\frac{U^3}{\ell}\big(1+\Rey^{-1}+\Rey_N^{-1}\big)$, where $\Rey_N=UL^{2N+1}/ν_N$ is the relaxation Reynolds number. We then develop a K41-type similarity theory. The model's micro-scale solves an explicit scalar equation, which has no solution below a threshold value of $χ$ and two solutions above it; the larger one is the cut-off scale. Requiring the micro-scale to equal the filter radius gives the scaling $χ\simeq U(δ/L)^{1/3}(1+1/α)^{N+1}$, for which the consistency error of the relaxation term is $O(δ^{2N+4/3})$ uniformly in $α$.

papers.title: Periodic orbits 1-5 of quadratic polynomials on a new coordinate plane
papers.abstract: While iterating the quadratic polynomial f_{c}(x)=x^{2}+c the degree of the iterates grows very rapidly, and therefore solving the equations corresponding to periodic orbits becomes very difficult even for periodic orbits with a low period. In this work we present a new iteration model by introducing a change of variables into an (u,v)-plane, which changes situation drastically. As an excellent example of this we can compare equations of orbits period four on (x,c)- and (u,v)-planes. In the latter case, this equation is of degree two with respect to u and it can be solved explicitly. In former case the corresponding equation ((((x^{2}+c)^{2}+c)^{2}+c)^{2}+c-x)/((x^{2}+c)^{2}+c-x)=0 is of degree 12 and it is thus much more difficult to solve.

papers.title: The variety of $2$-dimensional algebras over an algebraically closed field
papers.abstract: The work is devoted to the variety of $2$-dimensional algebras over an algebraically closed field. Firstly, we classify such algebras modulo isomorphism. Then we describe the degenerations and the closures of principal algebra series in the variety under consideration. Finally, we apply our results to obtain analogous descriptions for the subvarieties of flexible and bicommutative algebras. In particular, we describe rigid algebras and irreducible components for these subvarieties.

papers.title: The retarded interaction and non-scattering for 3D Maxwell--Dirac system
papers.abstract: We prove an a priori obstruction to linear scattering for the massive Maxwell--Dirac system in three space dimensions. A global solution with nonzero charge cannot scatter linearly in $L^2$ if its full and homogeneous potentials are $O(t^{-1})$, and the homogeneous potential is $o(t^{-1})$ in compact timelike cones. No nonlinear asymptotic expansion is assumed in this non-scattering theorem. We also identify the exact leading interaction when the nonlinear current approaches a free Dirac current in $L^1$. Its coefficient is a positive quadratic form in the velocity density and is bounded below by the square of the charge divided by $4π$. The proof uses free Dirac asymptotics and an estimate for retarded source errors after pairing with a smooth free current. The main arguments, including the oscillatory retarded interaction, are proved here. Global existence and the required nonlinear decay remain separate inputs; a small-data application to existing theory is stated explicitly as such.

papers.title: Homotopy type of equivariant embeddings
papers.abstract: We study spaces of symplectic embeddings of a closed four-ball into a closed symplectic four-manifold that are equivariant under a compact group action and centred on a component of the fixed point set. Adapting McDuff's argument, we reduce the path-connectedness of these spaces, and the uniqueness of equivariant blow-ups up to isotopy, to an equivariant deformation-to-isotopy statement on the blow-up. For compact abelian groups, we identify the stabilizer of a ball with the group of equivariant symplectomorphisms of the blow-up that preserve the exceptional divisor. For Hamiltonian circle actions on $\mathbb{C}P^2$, $S^2\times S^2$ and $\mathbb{C}P^2\#\overline{\mathbb{C}P^2}$, we obtain the invariant curves needed for inflation from toric extensions of the blown-up action, and we prove that the embedding spaces are path-connected. When the ball is centred at an isolated fixed point of $S^2\times S^2$ or $\mathbb{C}P^2\#\overline{\mathbb{C}P^2}$, the space of unparametrized balls is contractible or homotopy equivalent to $ΩS^3\times S^1$, according to the numbers of toric actions that extend the circle action and its blow-up. On $\mathbb{C}P^2$, it is homotopy equivalent to the fixed component. Along the way, we compute the centralizers of Hamiltonian circle actions on the one-point blow-up of $S^2\times S^2$, whose homotopy type depends only on the number of toric extensions.

papers.title: Scattering for cubic and Yukawa--Hartree Dirac equations wiith polynomially decaying spacetime metrics
papers.abstract: We study massive Dirac equations in three space dimensions with small, time-dependent perturbations of the principal coefficients and decaying zeroth-order matrix terms. The principal perturbation and its spatial derivatives decay polynomially at rate $ρ>7/2$, and its first time derivative has one additional inverse spatial power. We prove small-data global well-posedness and scattering for local cubic nonlinearities in $H^s$, $s>1+5/(2(ρ-1))$, and for Yukawa--Hartree nonlinearities in $H^s$, $s>1/2+5/(2(ρ-1))$. The argument retains the coupling between the metric-adapted positive and negative branches. Its main ingredients are a time-independent modified energy, a weighted estimate controlling the full massive low-frequency component, and frequency-dependent spatial cutoffs. The operator class contains the geometric Dirac Hamiltonian of a synchronous spacetime metric with its full spin connection. No second time derivative, temporal integrability, or asymptotic stationarity is assumed. Scattering is formulated relative to the exact nonautonomous linear evolution.

papers.title: The Ulam sequence grows subexponentially
papers.abstract: We prove that the $n$-th element of the Ulam sequence, a somewhat mysterious recursively-defined sequence of positive integers, has size $e^{O(\sqrt{n})}$; previous upper bounds were exponential in $n$. Our argument uses an additive-combinatorial lemma, possibly of independent interest, about covering finite difference sets with multiplicatively short intervals. The proofs are due to ChatGPT.

papers.title: Annihilation versus anchoring of a topologically charged pair on a perforated two-dimensional surface
papers.abstract: Two independent random walks of opposite topological charge move on the discrete torus $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^2$, which contains $k$ well-separated holes. The walks annihilate when they come within a core distance of each other, and each walk is anchored when it first touches a hole. We prove that the probability of annihilation before anchoring converges to $w_0/(w_0+\sum_j w_j)$, where the weights are explicit and depend only logarithmically on the sizes of the core and of the holes; for point-like core and holes, the limit is $1/(1+k)$. We then prove a fate theorem: the pair either terminates or ends as two opposite charges anchored on two different holes, with probability $(k-1)/(k+1)$ in the point-like case, and the hosting pair $\{j,l\}$ is chosen with probability proportional to $w_jw_l$. The proof combines an abstract competition lemma for rare sets in reversible Markov chains with sharp two-dimensional Green's function estimates.

papers.title: Commuting pairs in lattices of reductive Lie algebras
papers.abstract: We count ordered commuting pairs in a full lattice \(Λ\) in a reductive Lie algebra \(\g\) over \(\Q\). For a fixed convex body \(B\) containing the origin in its interior, the count in \(HB\) is \(C_{Λ,B}H^{\dim\g+\dim Z(\g)}\) with a power-saving error. The leading term comes from pairs whose projections to each simple ideal are linearly dependent over its centroid. Their slopes index an absolutely convergent sum of section volumes for \(C_{Λ,B}\). Subtracting the contribution of dependent pairs from the finite-field Fourier sums gives cancellation at generic dependent frequencies. For independent frequencies, we bound the dimension of the locus where the corresponding hyperplane contains an irreducible component of a nonzero bracket fibre. For \(n\ge3\), the number of ordered commuting pairs in \(M_n(\Z)\) with entries of absolute value at most \(H\) is \[ \frac{2(n+3)ζ(n^2-2)}{(n+1)ζ(n^2-1)} (2\lfloor H\rfloor+1)^{n^2+1} +O_n\!\left(H^{n^2+1-1/(n+1)}\right), \] confirming the exponent \(n^2+1\) predicted by Browning, Sawin and Wang~\cite{BSW}.

papers.title: A proof of the Jamneshan-Tao conjecture by embedding nilspaces in nilmanifolds
papers.abstract: We prove that every compact finite-rank nilspace admits a continuous injective morphism into a toral nilspace of the same step, and hence into a connected filtered nilmanifold. Combining this embedding theorem with the general nilspace inverse theorem, we establish the Jamneshan-Tao conjecture and extend its conclusion to second-countable compact abelian groups. This yields an inverse theorem for Gowers norms on all such groups, in which the correlating functions factor through morphisms into nilmanifolds. The proof relies on substantial foundations developed in nilspace theory over the past decade, particularly the general nilspace inverse theorem and the representation of compact finite-rank nilspaces as quotients of free nilspaces.

papers.title: Freeness of crossed modules, augmented quandles, and augmented racks
papers.abstract: We study freeness of crossed modules, augmented quandles, and augmented racks. We show that the associated quandle functor and the associated crossed module functor are left adjoint to the natural forgetful functors. For a map $f\colon S\to G$, we define the free augmented rack $R_f\to G$ and the free augmented quandle $Q_f\to G$. If $C_f\to G$ denotes the free crossed module determined by $f$, then the associated crossed modules of $R_f$ and $Q_f$ are both isomorphic to $C_f\to G$. We also characterize free augmented quandles in terms of stabilizers. As applications, we prove that the canonical inner augmentation of every generalized Alexander quandle is free and that the canonical inner augmentation of a classical knot quandle is free if and only if the knot is a torus knot, whereas for every $n$-knot with $n\geq2$ it is free.

papers.title: End-line Fourier restriction for hyperbolic surfaces in three dimensions
papers.abstract: We prove new bilinear adjoint Fourier restriction estimates for pairs of separated rectangles associated to a hyperbolic surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$. We then employ these bilinear estimates to prove Fourier extension inequalities along the (sharp) parabolic scaling line for any smooth hyperbolic 2-surface that is either the graph of a polynomial or that obeys a mild finite type condition.

papers.title: Weak Generators in Stable Module Categories
papers.abstract: The aim of this note is to show that the existence of weak generators in the stable module category of a ring, or equivalently, of $p$-indigent modules in the terminology of Holston et al., depends on the underlying model of set theory.

papers.title: Riemannian geodesic motions and null foliations
papers.abstract: We study the non-collision problem: given a unit vector field $V$ on a complete Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$, under what conditions on $V$ are the maps $F_t(p)=\exp_p(tV(p))$ injective for all $t\in\mathbb{R}$? If such a vector field exists, we call it a geodesic motion on $M$. This occurs, for instance, when $V$ defines a geodesic foliation of $M$, in which case, the geodesic motion is called stationary. We show that geodesic motions on the Euclidean plane are necessarily stationary, that generic geodesic motions on round spheres are non-stationary, and that compact hyperbolic $3$-manifolds admit no geodesic motions. The non-collision problem has a Lorentzian interpretation: geodesic motions on $M$ correspond to one-dimensional null geodesic foliations of the spacetime $(M\times\mathbb{R},g-dt^2)$. In the second part of the paper, we focus on codimension-one lightlike geodesic foliations of anti-de Sitter space $\operatorname{AdS}^{1,n}$. We give a complete characterization of such foliations by means of causal curves in the Einstein universe and prove rigidity in the projective anti-de Sitter case. The last part of the paper is dedicated to the study of one-dimensional geodesic foliations of $\operatorname{AdS}^{1,2}$. We give a complete characterization when the foliation contains at least one timelike leaf.

papers.title: The Triangular Abrikosov Constant and the Thomas--Fermi $Γ$-Limit of Rotating Bose--Einstein Condensates
papers.abstract: We resolve the Abrikosov coefficient conjecture for rapidly rotating two-dimensional Bose--Einstein condensates within the variational framework of $Γ$-convergence. For a harmonic trap, we establish the $Γ$-convergence of the rescaled Gross--Pitaevskii energy functionals in the fast-rotation regime, through weak $L^2$ convergence of the rescaled densities, and identify the effective interaction coefficient $β_*$ with $b_\triangle$, the Abrikosov ratio associated with the triangular vortex lattice. The limiting Thomas--Fermi functional determines the first correction to the minimum energy and the macroscopic density of almost minimizers. For the auxiliary rescaled model and its lowest-Landau-level restriction, we also compute a strictly positive limiting $L^2$ distance between minimizing densities and the Thomas--Fermi profile. The identification of the effective interaction coefficient $β_*$ with the triangular Abrikosov ratio $b_\triangle$ relies on the sharp Gaussian-minorant theorem established in a recent OpenAI preprint~\cite[Theorem~1.2]{Atomic}. A Fourier representation of the quartic energy and a weighted Poisson identity yield a lower bound for arbitrary magnetic-periodic lowest-Landau-level states. The sign conditions on the minorant and its Fourier transform give the bound, while the lattice contact conditions identify its coefficient with $b_\triangle$. Cutoff and magnetic projection transfer this estimate to local holomorphic states without boundary conditions or periodicity assumptions. Consequently, the free-cell coefficients converge to $b_\triangle$ with error $O(L^{-1/5})$ on squares of side length $L$.

papers.title: On the Hofer-Zehnder conjecture for Reeb flows without symmetry
papers.abstract: This paper continues our investigation of the Hofer-Zehnder conjecture for dynamically convex, non-degenerate Reeb pseudo-rotations of $S^{2n-1}$. The main result of the paper is that, for $n\geq 3$, such a flow has at most $n-3$ alternating prime closed orbits and hence at most $2n-3$ prime closed orbits in total. In particular, the flow on $S^5$ has exactly three prime closed orbits, all of which are non-alternating and elliptic. In addition, we prove that a dynamically convex Reeb pseudo-rotation on a sphere has at least two non-degenerate, irrationally elliptic orbits.

papers.title: Gusto: a toolkit for compatible finite element dynamical cores
papers.abstract: Gusto is a tool for rapid prototyping of new algorithms based on compatible finite element methods for discretising the fluid equations in the dynamical core of weather and climate models. In this context, the development of new algorithms typically follows a path that involves testing on a hierarchy of simpler equation sets sharing important features of the mathematical structure of the equation set solved by the dynamical core. Gusto provides compatible finite element spatial discretisations of the hierarchy of equation sets, along with a range of timestepping schemes. The code is modular so that different spatial and temporal discretisations can be combined and the same schemes can be applied to any of the equation sets. This facilitates fair comparison of the schemes and makes the extension of any algorithmic developments to the more complex equation sets more straightforward. In this paper we present Gusto to the community by describing the algorithms implemented in Gusto and showcasing their performance through a variety of test problems commonly used in numerical weather prediction.

papers.title: A new tautological relation on $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{2,14}$ in cohomology
papers.abstract: We construct a relation $\mathsf{Q}$ in the cohomological tautological ring $\mathsf{RH}^*(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{2,14})$ which lies outside the space of $3$-spin relations. $\mathsf{Q}$ is a simple linear combination of pure boundary strata classes of codimension 9 supported on the divisor $Δ_0 \subset \overline{\mathcal{M}}_{2,14}$ of irreducible nodal curves, and transforms according to the irreducible representation of $Σ_{14}$ associated to the partition $(2^7)$. The result shows that the set of $3$-spin relations cannot be complete in cohomology. Motivic conjectures relating algebraic cycles to special values of $L$-functions suggest that $\mathsf{Q}$ is nonzero in Chow. More precisely, we prove that the Chow nonvanishing of $\mathsf{Q}$ follows from a conjecture of Harder concerning the failure of the Manin--Drinfeld principle in genus 2. We prove that $\mathsf{Q}$ vanishes in cohomology by pairing with generators of the tautological ring. To prove $\mathsf{Q}$ is not in the set of $3$-spin relations requires an argument involving the $Σ_{14}$-representation-theoretic properties of the $3$-spin relations and the cohomology of local systems on $\mathcal{A}_2$ and $\mathcal{M}_2$. Parallel constructions for other moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n}$ are discussed in the paper. There are many open questions.

papers.title: Extrinsic Representation of the Partial Ricci Flow
papers.abstract: The partial Ricci flow (PRF) modifies the Riemannian metric on a foliation on a distribution orthogonal to the leaves. In this work we develop extrinsic representations of PRF on geodesic foliations (twisted/warped products, weak K-contact and weak \b{eta}-Kenmotsu manifolds) and analyze model cases where PRF admits closed-form solutions. Using the convergence of PRF on model cases, we construct its extrinsic representations initialized by rotational hypersurfaces in Euclidean space as well as parallel curved surfaces and ellipsoids. The extrinsic viewpoint for PRF provides new tools for studying curvature-driven dynamics on foliations, with potential applications to calculus of moving surfaces and mathematical physics.

papers.title: Sampling recovery for intersections of Lipschitz classes in the low-smoothness regime
papers.abstract: We study sampling recovery in $L_p(\mathbb T^d)$ for intersections of Lipschitz classes defined by smoothness conditions in two different metrics $L_p$ and $L_q$, where $1\le p<q\le\infty$. Our focus is on the low-smoothness range, where the $L_p$-smoothness does not exceed the classical continuity threshold $d/p$. We determine the exact orders of the sampling numbers for both linear and general recovery algorithms, including critical smoothness cases in which logarithmic factors appear or uniform convergence fails. To analyze sampling approximation in the low-smoothness range, we establish new inequalities for averaged moduli of smoothness with different integrability parameters and derive sharp estimates for these moduli and the corresponding semi-discrete measures of smoothness. These estimates provide error bounds for linear sampling operators acting on functions whose smoothness may lie below the classical continuity threshold. Finally, we determine the Kolmogorov widths of the intersection classes and quantify the gap between optimal sampling recovery and approximation by finite-dimensional subspaces.

papers.title: Generalized Power Graph of a Group
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new class of graphs, called generalized power graphs, and investigate some of their key properties, such as completeness, connectivity, and planarity.

papers.title: Cartan Dynamics and Limit Sets on Flag Manifolds
papers.abstract: The classical convergence principle describes the collapse of the Riemann sphere under divergent sequences of Möbius transformations. We develop its counterpart for arbitrary real semisimple Lie groups acting on flag manifolds, and use it to study limit sets and domains of discontinuity of discrete subgroups. The key is to let the source move: the destination of $x$ under $(g_m)$ is the set of all limits of $g_mx_m$ with $x_m\to x$. Our destination formula computes it as the closure of a unipotent orbit, determined by the Cartan data and a bounded Levi factor. The stratified convergence principle organises these destinations into families of translated Schubert varieties attached to boundary points of a compactification of the group. Over the complex numbers, the destination relation is the support of Brion's limiting graphs in the wonderful compactification, providing scheme structures, multidegrees and diagonal intersections. For discrete groups, the union of destination relations determines proper discontinuity and whether a largest domain exists. It relates Quint's flag limit set, Conze--Guivarc'h, Kulkarni and Myrberg sets to the recurrent set, while balanced choices of cells yield domains for every discrete subgroup, without Anosov hypotheses. For symmetric-power actions of non-elementary Kleinian groups on $\mathbb{CP}^N$, we compute the largest domain by a multiplicity bound at points of the classical limit set; for $N\ge3$ it strictly contains the Kulkarni domain, which equals the equicontinuity region. We also obtain nonempty largest domains for Zariski-dense cusped Hitchin groups with unipotent elements, and examples of strongly irreducible groups with no largest domain.

papers.title: Correlation distribution for a class of Niho exponents via self-conjugate-reciprocal polynomials and Kloosterman sums
papers.abstract: Let $q=2^m$ for an even $m\geq 6$ and let $d=s(q-1)+1$ with $4s\equiv5\pmod{q+1}$. In this paper, the correlation distribution between a binary m-sequence of period $q^2-1$ and its $d$-decimation is considered. The cross-correlation function takes seven values $q(i-1)-1$ for $0\leq i\leq 6$, and we determine their frequencies based on the study of low-degree self-conjugate-reciprocal polynomials and three mixed Kloosterman sums, which are finally expressed in terms of $K_m(1)$ and $K_m(ω)$, where $K_m(\cdot)$ is the Kloomsterman sum on the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$ and $ω$ is a primitive element of $\mathbb{F}_4$.

papers.title: Learning monotone game-theoretic linear MPC
papers.abstract: We propose a method to learn a game-theoretic model predictive control (GT-MPC) law by imitation from input and output data of a running multi-agent system. By interpreting the recorded inputs as the first moves of the equilibria of a game played by the agents, we learn the GT-MPC weights under hard input constraints and soft output constraints, without requiring the agents to reveal their objectives. We also impose that the resulting generalized Nash equilibrium (GNE) problem is strongly monotone, which ensures the existence and uniqueness of the equilibrium and, hence, that the learned GT-MPC law is well defined and can be evaluated efficiently online by variational GNE-seeking algorithms for linear-quadratic games. Moreover, strong monotonicity implies that the equilibrium is almost everywhere differentiable with respect to the references and the weights, which enables automatic differentiation for gradient-based optimization. In addition, we promote closed-loop stability of the unconstrained equilibrium feedback by incorporating a penalty that involves a jointly learned quadratic Lyapunov function. Learning a GT-MPC formulation enables us to explain the agents' objectives, reproduce their behavior in simulation in new scenarios, optimize their set-points, design mechanisms, and enforce additional constraints. A numerical example illustrates the approach.

papers.title: Multifidelity Operator Inference for Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: This paper presents a multifidelity (MF) formulation of Operator Inference (OpInf) for learning non-intrusive, physics-based reduced-order models (ROMs) of nonlinear dynamical systems. OpInf learns reduced operators from projections of snapshot data by solving a least squares regression problem. However, generating high-fidelity snapshots can be computationally expensive, limiting parameter coverage and the temporal extent of training trajectories for many aerospace applications, which can lead to inaccurate or unstable ROM predictions. This work proposes MF-OpInf, which combines limited high-fidelity snapshots with more plentiful low-fidelity snapshots through a control-variates-inspired MF least squares formulation to learn a single set of reduced operators across multiple trajectories. Low-fidelity trajectories provide additional parameter coverage and extend beyond the high-fidelity training time horizon. The low-fidelity snapshots are also used to construct an improved reduced basis through weighted proper orthogonal decomposition. We demonstrate MF-OpInf on a nonlinear reaction-diffusion problem with parametrized sinusoidal forcing and a two-dimensional incompressible flow past a cylinder with a parametrized inlet pulse. In these experiments, under an equal training simulation budget, MF-OpInf reduces the mean relative prediction error at unseen parameters by up to $87\%$ for the reaction-diffusion problem and $28\%$ for the cylinder flow problem over the test time regime, which extends beyond the high-fidelity training time horizon. These results demonstrate that MF-OpInf can improve temporal extrapolation and prediction at unseen parameters without increasing the training simulation budget.

papers.title: Wasserstein geometry of analytic cycle spaces
papers.abstract: We use optimal transport to define an intrinsic distance on connected components of the Barlet space of analytic cycles on a compact Kähler manifold, by associating to each cycle its normalized volume measure. We prove that any two cycles in the same connected component can be joined by a deformation of finite Wasserstein length, and that the resulting metric is complete and geodesic. On the locus of smooth reduced cycles at regular parameter points, Wasserstein lengths and energies coincide with those of the normalized Weil--Petersson metric. The construction thus gives a transport interpretation of Weil--Petersson geometry and extends beyond it to components containing no smooth reduced cycles.

papers.title: New Congruences for Simultaneously $l$-Regular and $t$-Distinct Partition in $k$-Colors
papers.abstract: Let $RD_{\ell,t}^k(n)$ enumerates the number of $k$-colored simultaneously $l$-regular and $t$-distinct partitions. In this article, we establish some new infinite families of congruences modulo prime $p$, $p\geq5$ and modulo powers of 5 for $RD_{\ell,t}^k(n)$. For instance, for each $n\geq0$, $0\leqα\leq{2k-2}$ and $k\geq1$, \begin{align*} \sum_{n=0}^{\infty}RD_{(5^{2k-1},5^{2k-1})}^2\big(5^{2k+α-1}n+\frac{9\cdot5^{2k+α-1}-2\cdot5^{2k-1}+1}{12}\big)q^n\equiv& 0\pmod{5^{k+\left[\fracα{2}\right]}} \end{align*}

papers.title: Noncommutative Rational Positivstellensätze with Operator Coefficients
papers.abstract: We establish a convex Positivstellensatz for noncommutative rational functions with bounded operator coefficients. A hermitian operator-valued rational function that is positive semidefinite on a matrix convex set described by a linear pencil admits a positivity certificate consisting of rational hermitian squares and a completely positive term involving the defining linear pencil. The certificate comes with an explicit complexity bound independent of the dimension of the coefficient Hilbert space. As a consequence, we solve the operator-valued noncommutative rational analog of Hilbert's 17th problem: every positive semidefinite operator-valued noncommutative rational function is a sum of hermitian squares, and even a single hermitian square when the coefficient Hilbert space is infinite-dimensional. In contrast, the corresponding commutative statement fails for infinite-dimensional operator coefficients.

papers.title: A graph discretization of the Steklov and Neumann problems on domains in complete Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative spectral convergence for graph discretizations of the Steklov and Neumann problems for bounded domains in complete Riemannian manifolds. Our construction uses weighted proximity graphs built from maximal $ε$-separated sets, with a correction to the discrete energy accounting for the geometry near the boundary. We consider two discrete Steklov problems: one defined using an averaged boundary trace, and the other using restriction to boundary vertices. Both approximate the continuum Steklov spectrum, but under different conditions on the discretization parameters. The additional scale condition required for the restriction-based problem is also necessary for spectral convergence. As a byproduct, we obtain quantitative convergence of the Neumann spectrum. The estimates are uniform under suitable geometric bounds.

papers.title: Isolation of $k$-cliques in uniform hypergraphs
papers.abstract: A copy of a hypergraph $F$ is called an $F$-copy. For any integers $k$ and $r$ with $2 \leq r \leq k$, let $K_k^r$ denote the complete $r$-uniform hypergraph whose vertex set is $[k] = \{1, 2, \dots, k\}$ (that is, the edges of $K_k^r$ are the $r$-element subsets of $[k]$). Given an $r$-uniform $m$-edge hypergraph $H$, the $K_k^r$-isolation number of $H$, denoted by $ι(H, K_k^r)$, is the size of a smallest subset $D$ of the vertex set of $H$ such that the closed neighbourhood $N[D]$ of $D$ intersects the vertex sets of the $K_k^r$-copies contained by $H$ (equivalently, $H-N[D]$ contains no $K_k^r$-copy). We prove that if $H$ is connected and not a $K_k^r$-copy, then $$ι(H, K^r_k) \le \left \lfloor \frac{(r-1)m + 1}{(r-1)(\binom{k}{r}+1) + 1} \right \rfloor.$$ The bound is best possible. This is a solution to a problem of Li, Zhang and Ye. We also provide an alternative proof for $r < k$. Both proofs introduce new ideas for establishing bounds on isolation parameters.
