A $d$-tilting bundle is a tilting bundle whose endomorphism algebra has global dimension at most $d$. The classification is motivated by dimer models, where internal perfect matchings give rise to $2$-representation infinite algebras. The algebras of type $\widetilde{A}$ introduced by Herschend, Iyama and Oppermann are higher-dimensional analogues in the simplex case. The same principle leads to a new class of algebras of type $\widetilde{A}\widetilde{A}$. Upper sets provide a common framework for tilting bundles, toric non-commutative crepant resolutions (NCCRs), and cuts of higher-dimensional dimer-type quivers. In the Picard-number-one case, the bundles are in bijection with non-trivial upper sets in the Picard group, and their endomorphism algebras are precisely $d$-representation infinite algebras of type $\widetilde{A}$. In the Picard-number-two case, a first upper set determines the ambient toric NCCR, and a second selects an internal cut of its quiver. This gives a complete classification of such $d$-tilting bundles and realizes their endomorphism algebras precisely as $d$-representation infinite algebras of type $\widetilde{A}\widetilde{A}$. The resulting geometric models give a combinatorial description of $d$-APR tilting modules and show that both classes of algebras are closed under $d$-APR tilts.

papers.title: Differential equations for intertwining operators among untwisted and twisted modules
papers.abstract: Given any vertex operator algebra $ V $ with an automorphism $ g $, we derive a Jacobi identity for an intertwining operator $ \mathcal{Y} $ of type $ \left( \begin{smallmatrix} W_3\\ W_1 \, W_2 \end{smallmatrix}\right) $ when $ W_1 $ is an untwisted $ V $-module, and $ W_2 $ and $ W_3 $ are $ g $-twisted $ V $-modules. We say such an intertwining operator is of $\left(\!\begin{smallmatrix} g\\ 1 \ g \end{smallmatrix}\!\right)$-type. Using the Jacobi identity, we obtain homogeneous linear differential equations satisfied by the multi-series $ \langle w_0, \mathcal{Y}_1(w_1,z_1) \cdots \mathcal{Y}_N(w_N,z_N) w_{N+1} \rangle $ when $ \mathcal{Y}_j $ are of $\left(\!\begin{smallmatrix} g\\ 1 \ g \end{smallmatrix}\!\right)$-type and the modules are $ C_1 $-cofinite and discretely graded. In the special case that $ V $ is an affine vertex operator algebra, we derive the ``twisted KZ equations" and show that its solutions have regular singularities at certain prescribed points when $ g $ has finite order. When $ V $ is general and $ g $ has finite order, we use the theory of regular singular points to prove that the multi-series $ \langle w_0, \mathcal{Y}_1(w_1,z_1) \cdots \mathcal{Y}_N(w_N,z_N) w_{N+1} \rangle $ converges absolutely to a multivalued analytic function when $ |z_1| > \cdots > |z_N| > 0 $ and analytically extends to the region $ z_i, z_i - z_j \neq 0 $. Furthermore, when $ N = 2 $, we show that these multivalued functions have regular singularities at certain prescribed points.

papers.title: Solving the BGK Model and Boltzmann equation by Fourier Neural Operator with conservative constraints
papers.abstract: The numerical approximation of the Boltzmann collision operator presents significant challenges because of its high dimensionality, quadratic nonlinearity, and nonlocal integral structure. In this work, we develop a Fourier Neural Operator (FNO)-based framework for learning finite time evolution operators associated with the spatially homogeneous Boltzmann equation and its simplified BGK model in different velocity space dimensions. The framework learns mappings between distribution functions in either sequence-to-sequence or point-to-point form and, once trained, enables rapid evaluation without repeated classical time evolution. To improve physical consistency, we introduce a conservative FNO (C-FNO) by augmenting the training loss with soft penalties for deviations in mass, momentum, and energy from the conservation law. Several numerical experiments are presented to demonstrate that the learned operators accurately reproduce the principal collision dynamics, while C-FNO generally reduces macroscopic drift relative to the standard FNO, highlighting its potential as a promising framework for physics-constrained operator learning in kinetic theory and other nonlinear integro-differential equations.

papers.title: Simultaneous Learning and Optimization via Misspecified Saddle Point Problems
papers.abstract: We study a class of misspecified saddle point (SP) problems, where the optimization objective depends on an unknown parameter that must be learned concurrently from data. Unlike existing studies that assume parameters are fully known or pre-estimated, our framework integrates optimization and learning into a unified formulation, enabling a more flexible problem class. To address this setting, we propose two algorithms based on the accelerated primal-dual (APD) by Hamedani & Aybat 2021. In particular, we first analyze the naive extension of the APD method by directly substituting the evolving parameter estimates into the primal-dual updates; then, we design a new learning-aware variant of the APD method that explicitly accounts for parameter dynamics by adjusting the momentum updates. Both methods achieve a provable convergence rate of $\mathcal{O}(\log K / K)$, while the learning-aware approach attains a tighter $\mathcal{O}(1)$ constant and further benefits from an adaptive step-size selection enabled by a backtracking strategy. Furthermore, we extend the framework to problems where the learning problem admits multiple optimal solutions, showing that our modified algorithm for a structured setting achieves an $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{K})$ rate. To demonstrate practical impact, we evaluate our methods on a misspecified portfolio optimization problem and show superior empirical performance compared to state-of-the-art algorithms.

papers.title: On a fractional Alt-Caffarelli-Friedman-type monotonicity formula
papers.abstract: In this paper, by exploiting mean value properties of $s$-harmonic functions, we introduce some monotonicity formulas in the nonlocal setting. Our approach is purely nonlocal and does not rely on the extension technique. As a byproduct we also establish interior nonlocal gradient estimates and a nonlocal analogue of the Bochner identity.

papers.title: Inverse Reinforcement Learning with Just Classification and a Few Regressions
papers.abstract: Inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) seeks to recover a reward function from observed behavior, but rewards are typically only partially identified: many reward--value pairs can induce the same behavior policy. We study this problem in the maximum-entropy, or Gumbel-shock, model under a broad class of statewise affine normalization constraints, with anchor-action constraints as a special case. This leads to Generalized Policy-to-$Q$-to-Reward (GenPQR), a modular approach to normalized reward recovery based on policy estimation and $Q$-evaluation via the Bellman equation; both components can be instantiated with off-the-shelf classification and regression methods. We establish modular finite-sample guarantees under general function approximation, with separate terms for policy-estimation and $Q$-function estimation error. We also give explicit bounds for GenPQR with fitted $Q$-evaluation. In experiments, GenPQR improves on DeepPQR in reward recovery. Our guarantees extend beyond anchor actions, accommodate large action spaces, and are not tied to a specific neural-network architecture or training procedure.

papers.title: Brauer groups of certain affine cubic surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the Brauer groups of affine surfaces that are complements of singular hyperplane sections of smooth cubic surfaces over a field $k$ of characteristic $0$. We determine the Brauer group over the algebraic closure as a Galois module for all the possible singular hyperplane sections. For the case when the hyperplane section is geometrically the union of three lines, we give explicit examples where transcendental elements of order $2$ and $3$ exist over $\mathbb{Q}$. We end with an explicit example of an integral Brauer--Manin obstruction to the Hasse principle given by an element of order~$3$ on an affine cubic surface with singular boundary.

papers.title: Spectral gaps and uniqueness in the isotropic $L_p$ Minkowski problem
papers.abstract: We investigate the isotropic $L_p$ Minkowski problem in $\mathbb{R}^n$ for $p<-n$. We prove that a smooth strictly convex solution $K$ is the unit ball if the second non-zero eigenvalue of the Hilbert-Brunn-Minkowski operator satisfies $λ_2(-L_K)\ge\frac{-p-1}{n-1}$. We also derive a lower bound for $λ_2(-L_K)$ in terms of concentric inner and outer ellipsoids and give improved bounds for origin-centred and origin-symmetric bodies. Combined with a weighted centroid identity for the polar body, these estimates yield an explicit $\varepsilon_n>0$ for which the unit ball is the only solution when $-n-\varepsilon_n\le p<-n$.

papers.title: Model Order Reduction for Quantum Molecular Dynamics
papers.abstract: Quantum molecular dynamics (QMD) provides a high-fidelity physical framework for modeling atomic and molecular phenomena from first principles. However, its mathematical formulation requires solving iterative, high-dimensional electronic structure problems at every physical state step. Within the broader data-driven computational mechanics paradigm, we present a projection-based model order reduction framework for electronic structure calculation in QMD. By discovering a low-dimensional manifold of the electronic solution space within Kohn-Sham density functional theory, our approach projects the governing variational formulation onto an intrinsically reduced subspace. This avoids full-space iterative wavefunction optimization while preserving rigorous physical symmetries and state consistency. We demonstrate this methodology on a water molecule, demonstrating strong agreement with high-fidelity reference solutions across structural trajectories and thermodynamic observables through canonical coordinate alignment and structured manifold sampling.

papers.title: An interpolation of Bradley's sum formula
papers.abstract: The sum formula for $q$-multiple zeta values is a well-known relation. In this paper, we present its generalization for the $q$-multiple zeta function.

papers.title: Augmentation categories in higher dimensions
papers.abstract: For an exact symplectic manifold $M$ and a Legendrian submanifold $Λ$ of the contactification $M\times \mathbb{R}$, we construct the augmentation category (over a field of characteristic 2), a unital $A_\infty$-category whose objects are augmentations of the Chekanov-Eliashberg differential graded algebra. This extends the construction of the augmentation category by Ng-Rutherford-Shende-Sivek-Zaslow to contact manifolds of dimension greater than 3.

papers.title: Fully implicit timestepping methods for the rotating shallow water equations
papers.abstract: Fully implicit timestepping methods have had limited application in geophysical fluid dynamics due to challenges of finding suitable iterative solvers, since the coupled treatment of advection prevents the standard elimination techniques. However, overlapping Additive Schwarz methods provide a robust, scalable iterative approach for solving the monolithic coupled system for all fields and Runge-Kutta stages. In this study we investigate this approach applied to the rotating shallow water equations, facilitated by the Irksome package which provides automated code generation for implicit Runge-Kutta methods. We compare various schemes in terms of accuracy and efficiency using an implicit/explicit splitting method, namely the ARK2 scheme of Giraldo et al (2013), as a benchmark. This provides an initial look at whether implicit Runge-Kutta methods can be viable for atmosphere and ocean simulation.

papers.title: Semi-infinite parabolic IC-sheaf II: the Ran space version
papers.abstract: This paper is a sequel to arXiv:2310.0638. Let G be a split reductive group. We define the parabolic semi-infinite category on the Ran version of the affine Grassmanian Gr_{G,Ran}. We study the semi-infinite parabolic IC-sheaf in this category. We provide several descriptions of this object, one as certain colimit, another as an intermediate extension in certain category. We relate the global and local semi-infinite categories of sheaves. We also relate the intersection cohomology sheaf of the Drinfeld compactification of Bun_P with the semi-infinite parabolic IC-sheaf.

papers.title: On the Nyquist Criterion and the Scaled Relative Graph for SISO systems: A Generalized Circle Criterion
papers.abstract: Scaled Relative Graphs (SRGs) provide a novel graphical frequency-domain method for the analysis of nonlinear systems. However, existing SRG-based methods are limited to stable open-loop dynamics and can lead to false conclusions when applied to unstable Linear and Time-Invariant (LTI) components. In this paper, we identify the source of this pitfall and resolve it by introducing the extended SRG, which augments the SRG of an LTI system with the encirclement information of the Nyquist criterion. We show how the extended SRG can be used for stability and $H_\infty$-performance analysis of LTI systems and the computation of SRGs for unstable LTI systems. Building on these results, we derive graphical stability and incremental $L_2$-gain conditions for three canonical nonlinear feedback interconnections: the Lur'e system, the controlled Lur'e system, and an LTI plant with Lur'e controller. As a corollary, we derive a user-friendly generalized circle criterion that relates the $L_2$-gain directly to separation between the Nyquist curve and the critical disk from the classical circle criterion, requiring SRGs only for the proof, not its statement. The proposed approach is validated on several examples involving unstable LTI dynamics and nonlinearities, demonstrating applicability beyond the capabilities of existing SRG methods.

papers.title: Diophantine equations in matrix rings and semirings
papers.abstract: For every fixed positive integer $n$, we prove that it is undecidable whether a single noncommutative polynomial equation with scalar integer coefficients has a solution in $M_n(\mathbb N)$ or in $M_n(\mathbb Z)$. An integral range calculation for central polynomials yields a common reduction from integer Diophantine equations; the single-equation and finite-system problems are computably enumerable complete. The same polynomials have exact range $\mathbb Q I_n$ on rational, even nonnegative rational, arguments. Consequently, the single-equation and finite-system problems over $M_n(\mathbb Q)$ are computably many-one equivalent to Hilbert's tenth problem over $\mathbb Q$, unconditionally. The rational undecidability claims reported in 2026 by OpenAI and Zhi-Wei Sun imply rational-matrix undecidability, with at most $86$, $87$, and $88$ matrix variables in dimensions $1$, $2$, and at least $3$, respectively. An explicit Diophantine definition of $\mathbb Z$ in $\mathbb Q$ reported by the project coordinated by Elliot Glazer further gives completeness among computably enumerable problems. These consequences of recent arithmetic claims are stated conditionally.

papers.title: Exponentially Fading Memory Signature
papers.abstract: We introduce the exponentially fading memory (EFM) signature, a time-invariant transformation of an infinite (possibly rough) path that serves as a mean-reverting analogue of the classical path signature. We construct the EFM-signature via rough path theory, carefully adapted to accommodate improper integration from minus infinity. The EFM-signature retains many of the key algebraic and analytical properties of classical signatures, including a suitably modified Chen identity, the linearization property, path-determinacy, and the universal approximation property. From the probabilistic perspective, the EFM-signature provides a "stationarized" representation, making it particularly well-suited for time-series analysis and signal processing overcoming the shortcomings of the standard signature. In particular, the EFM-signature of time-augmented Brownian motion evolves as a group-valued Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process. We establish its stationarity, Markov property, and exponential ergodicity in the Wasserstein distance, and we derive an explicit formula à la Fawcett for its expected value in terms of Magnus expansions. We also study linear combinations of EFM-signature elements and the computation of associated characteristic functions in terms of a mean-reverting infinite dimensional Riccati equation.

papers.title: Hodge-Riemann polynomials
papers.abstract: We show that Schur classes of ample vector bundles on smooth projective varieties satisfy Hodge--Riemann relations on $H^{p,q}$ under the assumption that $H^{p-2,q-2}$ vanishes. More generally, we study Hodge--Riemann polynomials, which are partially symmetric polynomials that produce cohomology classes satisfying the Hodge--Riemann property when evaluated at Chern roots of ample vector bundles. In the case of line bundles and in bidegree $(1,1)$, these are precisely the nonzero dually Lorentzian polynomials. We prove various properties of Hodge--Riemann polynomials, confirming predictions and answering questions of Ross and Toma. As an application, we deduce Schur log-concavity of derivative sequences of products of Schur polynomials, confirming conjectures of Ross and Wu. We also prove monomial log-concavity of derivative sequences of dually Lorentzian polynomials. In an appendix, Shouda Wang uses this result to give a new proof of the Dowling--Zhao conjecture.

papers.title: On the Convergence Rates of Iterative Regularization Algorithms for Composite Bilevel Optimization
papers.abstract: This paper investigates iterative methods for solving bilevel optimization problems where both inner and outer functions have a composite structure. We establish novel theoretical results, including the first analysis that provides simultaneous convergence rates for the Iteratively REgularized Proximal Gradient (IRE-PG) method, a variant of Solodov's algorithm. These rates for the inner and outer functions highlight the inherent trade-offs between their respective convergence behaviors. We further extend this analysis to an accelerated version of IRE-PG, proving faster convergence rates under specific settings. Additionally, we propose a new scheme for handling cases where these methods cannot be directly applied to the bilevel problem due to the difficulty of computing the associated proximal operator. This scheme offers surrogate functions to approximate the original problem and a framework to translate convergence rates between the surrogate and original functions. Our results show that the accelerated method's advantage diminishes under this translation.

papers.title: Dissipative solutions for 2D Onsager's conjecture
papers.abstract: In 1949, L. Onsager conjectured that weak solutions of the Euler equations in $C_{t,x}^γ$ are energy conservative when $γ>\frac{1}{3}$, whereas nonconservative solutions exist when $γ<\frac{1}{3}$. Constantin, E and Titi [13] proved the conservation part, while Isett [26] constructed nontrivial $C^γ_{t,x}$ weak solutions with compact support in time in three dimensions for each $0<γ<\frac{1}{3}$. Building on this breakthrough work, Buckmaster, De Lellis, Székelyhidi Jr. and Vicol [7] obtained strictly dissipative solutions below the Onsager threshold. In two dimensions, Giri and Radu [23] first constructed a nontrivial weak solution in $C^{\frac{1}{3}-}(\mathbb T^2\times[0,T])$ and left an open problem whether it would be possible to construct dissipative solutions (controllable energy) below $\frac{1}{3}$ threshold. In this paper, we reslove this question and thereby obtain infinitely many strictly dissipative weak solutions in $C^γ(\mathbb T^2\times[0,T])$ for every $0<γ<\frac{1}{3}$. Moreover, we prove that the associated wild initial data are dense in the divergence-free subspace of $C^{γ'}(\mathbb{T}^2)$ for any $0<γ' <\frac{1}{3}$. The key new ingredient is a family of staircase traveling waves, which we combine with a Picard iteration coupled to the Newton--Nash scheme to control both the Reynolds stress and the kinetic energy. The construction also applies in every dimension $d\geq2$.

papers.title: The mean curvature flow of subgroups on Lie groups of dimension three
papers.abstract: In this work we study the existence of solutions to the Mean Curvature Flow for which the initial condition has the structure of a two-dimensional Lie subgroup within a Lie group of dimension three. We consider Lie groups with a fixed left-invariant metric and first observe that if the Lie group is unimodular, then every Lie subgroup is a minimal surface (hence a trivial solution). For this reason we focus on non-unimodular Lie groups, finding the evolution of every Lie subgroup of dimension 2 (within a 3 dimensional Lie group). These evolutions are self-similar for abelian subgroups (i.e. evolve by isometries), but not self-similar in the other cases.

papers.title: Perfect weight divisibility of (fork, co-fork$\cup K_1$)-free graphs
papers.abstract: A {\em fork} is a graph obtained from $K_{1,3}$ (usually called {\em claw}) by subdividing an edge once, an {\em co-fork} is the complement graph of a fork, and a {\em co-cricket} is a union of $K_1$ and $K_4-e$. A graph is perfectly divisible if for each of its induced subgraphs $H$, $V (H)$ can be partitioned into $A$ and $B$ such that $H[A]$ is perfect and $ω(H[B]) < ω(H)$. A graph is perfectly weight divisible if the same condition holds for any positive integer weights on its vertices, using the maximum weight of a clique instead of the clique number. Sivaraman proposed the conjecture that every fork-free graph is perfectly divisible in a paper by Karthick {\em et al.} [Electron. J. Comb. 29 (2022), P3.19.]. In the same paper, they proved that every ((\text{fork},\text{co-cricket}))-free graph is either claw-free or perfectly divisible. In this paper, we show that every (fork, co-fork$\cup K_1$)-free graph is perfectly weight divisible, and hence perfectly divisible. This improves some results of Karthick {\em et al.}.

papers.title: $L^2$ extension of holomorphic functions in the general non-analytic setting
papers.abstract: In an influential $L^2$ extension theorem due to Demailly, the subvariety to extend from is defined by the multiplier ideal of a quasi-plurisubharmonic defining function with analytic singularities. In his theorem, the finiteness of an $L^2$ norm called the Ohsawa norm plays the crucial role of determining whether a given holomorphic function or section can be extended. In 2016, Demailly asked if the Ohsawa norm behaves equally well when the defining function is further generalized to admit non-analytic singularities. We answer this question negatively by showing that for a wide class of log canonical defining functions with a unique log canonical place, only the zero holomorphic function on the subvariety has finite Ohsawa norm. It follows that for such a defining function, the $L^2$ extension theorem is vacuous. This reveals a fundamental obstruction in the theory of $L^2$ extension in the general non-analytic setting.

papers.title: Optimizing the ground state energy of the three-dimensional magnetic Dirichlet Laplacian with constant magnetic field
papers.abstract: This paper concerns the shape optimization problem of minimizing the ground state energy of the magnetic Dirichlet Laplacian with constant magnetic field among three-dimensional domains of fixed volume. In contrast to the two-dimensional case, a generalized "magnetic" Faber-Krahn inequality does not hold and minimizers cannot be balls when the magnetic field is turned on. An analysis of the problem among cylindrical domains reveals geometric constraints for general minimizers. In particular, minimizers must elongate with a certain rate along the direction of the magnetic field as the field strength increases. In addition to the theoretical analysis, we present numerical minimizers which confirm this prediction and give rise to further conjectures.

papers.title: Symmetric compatibility of theta structures, with applications to change of level and isogenies
papers.abstract: Let $m,n,d >1$ be integers such that $n=md$ and let $(B, \mathscr{M}, Θ\_{\mathscr{M}})$ be a marked abelian variety of level $m$ over a field of odd characteristic. We study the theta structures of level $n$ for $\mathscr{M}^d$, and the theta structures on the abelian varieties $d$-isogenous to $B$, which are compatible with $Θ\_{\mathscr{M}}$. When $d$ is odd and coprime to $m$, they correspond to the isotropic subgroups of $B[n]$, and this correspondence underlies the known algorithms in theta coordinates. In general, this is no longer true. We introduce the notion of symmetric compatibility of a torsion point with a symmetric level subgroup, and we show that a subgroup of $B[n]$ isomorphic to $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^g$ comes from a compatible theta structure if and only if it is isotropic and all its points are symmetric compatible. We extend to every $d$ Mumford's notion of compatible pairs of theta structures, defined by Mumford for $d=2$, and prove that it is equivalent to our notion, which can be tested on theta coordinates; we also describe exactly the remaining ambiguity, which explains the sign choices met when the duplication formula is used to change the level. As applications, we obtain change of level and isogeny algorithms without assuming that $d$ is odd and coprime to $m$, using $O(n^{3g} \log(d))$ and $O(n^{2g} \log(d))$ operations in the base field respectively. In particular, they give change of level algorithms for even $d$, and $2$-isogenies in level $4$ theta coordinates with an explicit control of the theta structure of the codomain.

papers.title: A convex integration scheme for the continuity equation past the Sobolev embedding threshold
papers.abstract: We introduce a convex integration scheme for the continuity equation in the context of the Di Perna-Lions theory that allows to build incompressible vector fields in $C_{t}W^{1,p}_x$ and nonunique solutions in $C_{t} L^{q}_x$ for any $p,q$ with $\frac{1}{p} + \frac{1}{q} > 1 + \frac{1}{d}- δ$ for some $δ>0$. This improves the previous bound, corresponding to $δ=0$, or equivalently $q' > p^*$, obtained with convex integration so far, and critical for those schemes in view of the Sobolev embedding that guarantees that solutions are distributional in the opposite range.

papers.title: The threshold for loose Hamilton cycles in random hypergraph
papers.abstract: We show that w.h.p.\ the random $r$-uniform hypergraph $H_{n,m}$ contains a loose Hamilton cycle, provided $r\geq 3$ and $m\geq \frac{(1+ε)n\log n}{r}$, where $ε$ is an arbitrary positive constant. This is asymptotically best possible, as if $m\leq \frac{(1-ε)n\log n}{r}$ then w.h.p.\ $H_{n,m}$ contains isolated vertices.

papers.title: Asymptotic behavior of penalty dynamics for constrained variational inequalities
papers.abstract: We propose a comprehensive framework for solving constrained variational inequalities via various classes of evolution equations displaying multi-scale aspects. In an infinite-dimensional Hilbertian framework, the class of dynamical systems we propose combine Tikhonov regularization and exterior penalization terms in order to induce strong convergence of trajectories to least norm solutions in the constrained domain. Our construction thus unifies the literature on regularization methods and penalty-based dynamical systems. An extension to a full splitting formulation of the constrained domain is also provided, with associated weak convergence results involving the Attouch-Czarnecki condition.

papers.title: An 'Experimental Mathematics' Approach to Stolarsky Interspersions via Automata Theory
papers.abstract: We look at the Stolarsky interspersions (such as the Wythoff array) one more time, this time using tools from automata theory. These tools allow easy verification of many of the published results on these arrays, as well as proofs of new results.

papers.title: Leafwise positive scalar curvature and the Rosenberg index
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a closed spin manifold, in this paper, we show that if there is a foliation $(M,F)$ and a Riemannian metric on $M$ that has leafwise positive scalar curvature then the Rosenberg index of $M$ is zero.

papers.title: Numerical approximation of nonlinear fourth-order SPDEs with additive space-time white noise
papers.abstract: We consider the strong numerical approximation for a fourth-order stochastic nonlinear SPDE driven by space-time white noise on {$d=1,2,3$}-dimensional torus. We consider its full discretisation with a spectral Galerkin scheme in space and Euler scheme in time. We show the convergence with almost spatial rate $2-\frac{d}{2}$ and $\frac{6-d}{4} \wedge 1$-temporal rate obtained mainly via \it{Stochastic Sewing} technique.

papers.title: Efficient LP warmstarting for linear modifications of the constraint matrix
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of computing the optimal solution and objective value of a linear program whose constraint matrix changes linearly with a parameter, for a predefined set of values of this parameter. Based on the information given by a precomputed basis, we present three efficient LP warm-starting algorithms, based on the eigenvalue decomposition, the Schur decomposition and the Hessenberg decomposition, to evaluate the optimal solution and optimal objective value of these problems. The three algorithms have an overall complexity of $O(pm^2+pmn)$ where $m$ (resp. $n$) is the number of constraints (resp. variables) of the original problem and $p$ the number of parameter values after an initial preprocessing step. We also provide theorems related to the optimality conditions to verify when a basis is still optimal. When the perturbation of the basis matrix has a low rank $ρ$, as is often the case in practice, we then reduce all the computations to a $ρ\timesρ$ matrix built with $ρ$ solves with the factorization of the basis maintained by the simplex solver; with it, we compute, in each direction, an interval on which the basis is guaranteed to remain optimal, together with a bound on the objective. In practice, these intervals are close to the exact ones, and they remain useful for degenerate bases. We also propose a matrix-free method based on shifted Krylov subspaces. Numerical experiments on 398 instances built from real models, with up to 349,120 constraints, assess the accuracy, the cost and the range of applicability of all the methods. On the interval on which a basis remains optimal, once this interval is known, the low-rank and Krylov methods compute the optimal objective value 117 to 304 times faster than a warm start of the solver, in median.

papers.title: Colouring signed analogues of Kneser, Schrijver, and Borsuk graphs
papers.abstract: The Kneser signed graph $\KS(n,k)$, $k\leq n$, is the graph whose vertices are signed $k$-subsets of $[n]$ (i.e. $k$-subsets $S$ of $\{ \pm 1, \pm 2, \ldots, \pm n\}$ such that $S\cap (-S)=\emptyset$). Two vertices $A$ and $B$ are adjacent with a positive edge if $A\cap (-B)=\emptyset$ and with a negative edge if $A\cap B=\emptyset$. We prove that the balanced chromatic number of $\KS(n,k)$ is $n-k+1$. We then introduce the signed analogue of Schrijver graphs and show that choosing one representative from each antipodal pair of alternating signed $k$-sets gives a vertex-critical subgraph of $\KS(n,k)$ with respect to balanced colouring. For the Borsuk signed graph on $S^d$, we obtain balanced chromatic number $d+1$ for sufficiently small distance parameter and relate this equality to antipodal covers of the sphere. On $S^2$, spherical and projective covering bounds give three, four and six as the first successive values of the balanced chromatic number.

papers.title: Limits of harmonic functions on $\mathbb{Z}^d$
papers.abstract: We give an example of a sequence of positive harmonic functions on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d\geq 2$, that converges pointwise to a non-harmonic function.

papers.title: Mean--Variance Portfolio Selection by Continuous-Time Reinforcement Learning: Algorithms, Regret Analysis, and Empirical Study
papers.abstract: We study continuous-time mean--variance portfolio selection in markets where stock prices are diffusion processes driven by observable factors that are also diffusion processes, yet the coefficients of these processes are unknown. Based on the recently developed reinforcement learning (RL) theory for diffusion processes, we present a general data-driven RL approach that learns the pre-committed investment strategy directly without attempting to learn or estimate the market coefficients. For multi-stock Black--Scholes markets without factors, we further devise an algorithm and prove its performance guarantee by deriving a sublinear regret bound in terms of the Sharpe ratio. We then carry out an extensive empirical study implementing this algorithm to compare its performance and trading characteristics, evaluated under a host of common metrics, with a large number of widely employed portfolio allocation strategies on S\&P 500 constituents. The results demonstrate that the proposed continuous-time RL strategy is consistently among the best, especially in a volatile bear market, and decisively outperforms the model-based continuous-time counterparts by significant margins.

papers.title: Boundary value problems for 0-elliptic operators
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a manifold with boundary, and let $L$ be a 0-elliptic operator on X which is semi-Fredholm essentially surjective with infinite-dimensional kernel. Examples include Hodge Laplacians and Dirac operators on conformally compact manifolds. We construct left and right parametrices for L when supplemented with appropriate elliptic boundary conditions. The construction relies on a new calculus of pseudodifferential operators on functions over both $X$ and $\partial X$, which we call the "symbolic 0-calculus". This new calculus supplements the ordinary 0-calculus of Mazzeo--Melrose, enabling it to handle boundary value problems. In the original 0-calculus, operators are characterized as polyhomogeneous right densities on a blow-up of $X^2$. By contrast, operators in the symbolic 0-calculus are characterized (locally near each point of the boundary of the diagonal) as quantizations of polyhomogeneous symbols on appropriate blown-up model spaces.

papers.title: Low-degree colorings without non-essential arguments
papers.abstract: For the Hamming graph $H(n,q)$, where $q$ is a constant prime power and $n$ grows, we construct perfect colorings without non-essential arguments such that $n$ depends exponentially on the off-diagonal part of the quotient matrix. In particular, we construct unbalanced functions (in the case $q=2$, Boolean functions) such that the number of essential arguments depends exponentially on the degree of the function. Another framing of the main construction is that it gives a sequence of very regular functions (perfect colorings) whose number of essential arguments grows exponentially with respect to sensitivity. A classical result that connects sensitivity with the number of essential arguments in the binary ($q=2$) case is the Simon--Wegener theorem. We prove an analog of this theorem for an arbitrary $q$. Keywords: boolean functions, perfect colorings, equitable partitions, degree, sensitivity, essential arguments

papers.title: Cylinder decompositions on geometric armadillo tails
papers.abstract: We study a class of finite-area, infinite-type translation surfaces and construct an explicit cylinder decomposition on these surfaces. The cylinder decomposition contains a special curve which distinguishes it from cylinder decompositions in other periodic directions.

papers.title: Investigation about a statement equivalent to Riemann Hypothesis (RH) applied to Dirichlet primitive L functions
papers.abstract: We apply a known equivalence, for RH about Riemann Z function, to Dirichlet L functions with primitive characters. A key point is the study of positivity condition in phase derivative of primitive L functions. In order to write it in workable form it is crucial to extend Euler product to critical strip. By exploiting the concept of y-friable integers this task is accomplished. Afterward, by use of the ratio limit in P.N.T.,it is shown that this partial derivative expression cannot be negative along critical line. Fulfilling so the statement above. Then, if the mentioned equivalence is true, this implies that no off-critical line zeros are allowed for at least odd-primitive Dirichlet L functions.

papers.title: Nonlocal elliptic equations involving logarithmic Laplacian: Existence, non-existence and uniqueness results
papers.abstract: In this work, we study the existence, non-existence, and uniqueness results for nonlocal elliptic equations involving logarithmic Laplacian, and subcritical, critical, and supercritical logarithmic nonlinearities. The Poho\u zaev's identity and Díaz-Saa type inequality are proved, which are of independent interest and can be applied to a larger class of problems. Depending upon the growth of nonlinearities and regularity of the weight function, we study the small-order asymptotic of nonlocal weighted elliptic equations involving the fractional Laplacian of order $2s.$ We show that the least energy solutions of a weighted nonlocal problem with superlinear or sublinear growth converge to a nontrivial nonnegative least-energy solution of Brézis-Nirenberg type and logistic-type limiting problem respectively involving the logarithmic Laplacian.

papers.title: Information geometric regularization of unidimensional pressureless Euler equations yields global strong solutions
papers.abstract: Partial differential equations describing compressible fluids are prone to the formation of shock singularities, arising from faster upstream fluid particles catching up to slower, downstream ones. In geometric terms, this causes the deformation map to leave the manifold of diffeomorphisms. Information geometric regularization addresses this issue by changing the manifold geometry to make it geodesically complete. Empirical evidence suggests that this results in smooth solutions without adding artificial viscosity. This work makes a first step towards understanding this phenomenon rigorously, in the setting of the unidimensional pressureless Euler equations. It shows that their information geometric regularization has smooth global solutions. By establishing $Γ$-convergence of its variational description, it proves convergence of these solutions to entropy solutions of the nominal problem, in the limit of vanishing regularization parameter. A consequence of these results is that manifolds of unidimensional diffeomorphisms with information geometric regularization are geodesically complete.

papers.title: Combinatorics of generalized orthogonal polynomials of type $R_{II}$
papers.abstract: In 1995, Ismail and Masson introduced orthogonal polynomials of types \( R_I \) and \( R_{II} \), which are defined by specific three-term recurrence relations with additional conditions. Recently, Kim and Stanton found a combinatorial interpretation for the moments of orthogonal polynomials of type \( R_I \) in the spirit of the combinatorial theory of orthogonal polynomials due to Flajolet and Viennot. In this paper, we push this combinatorial model further to orthogonal polynomials of type \( R_{II} \). Moreover, we generalize orthogonal polynomials of type \( R_{II} \) by relaxing some of their conditions. We then prove a master theorem, which generalizes combinatorial models for moments of various types of orthogonal polynomials: classical orthogonal polynomials, Laurent biorthogonal polynomials, and orthogonal polynomials of types \( R_I \) and \( R_{II} \).

papers.title: Transformation of Stochastic Recursions and Critical Phenomena in the Analysis of the Athreya-Aldous-Shields Cascade and Related Mean Flow Equations
papers.abstract: We study the discounted branching random walk process introduced by Athreya (1985) and Aldous and Shields (1988), referred to as the Athreya-Aldous-Shields (AAS) cascade. This process can be viewed as an idealized version of the stochastic model introduced by Le Jan and Sznitman in 1997 for the Navier-Stokes equations. The AAS cascade exhibits phase transitions at the critical branching rates $α=1$ and $α=2$. These transitions are reflected in the behavior of the associated mean flow equation, a nonlocal ODE referred to as the $α$-Riccati equation. It is known that if $α>1$, the AAS cascade is explosive in the sense of infinitely many splittings in finite time, and the $α$-Riccati equation has at least two solutions. In this paper, we establish finer structural properties of an explosive AAS cascade and obtain a stronger non-uniqueness result. Namely, for each initial data in a certain range, the $α$-Riccati equation has an infinite family of distinct solutions parametrized by their convergence rates at infinity. Our approach exploits a simple transformation between the AAS cascade and its "linearized" counterpart, whose mean flow equation is precisely the well-studied pantograph equation. This transformation demonstrates how a relationship at the level of stochastic processes can reveal an otherwise hidden relationship at the level of mean flow equations.

papers.title: On the lower central series of a large family of non-periodic GGS-groups
papers.abstract: For an odd prime $p$, we fully determine the lower central series of a large family of non-periodic GGS-groups, which has a density of roughly $(\frac{p-1}{p})^2$ within all GGS-groups. We also describe the structure of the $\mathbb{F}_p$-Lie algebra associated to the lower central series of these groups. These results represent a major step forward in the knowledge of the lower central series of distinguished classes of branch groups, which to date was basically restricted to the Grigorchuk group. As part of our results, we obtain the exact values of the indices between consecutive terms of the lower central series, and we show that these groups, as well as their profinite completions, have lower central width equal to $2$. In particular, this confirms a conjecture of Bartholdi, Eick, and Hartung about the generalised Fabrykowski-Gupta groups.

papers.title: Inequalities characterizing distinguished unipotent orbits
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove a new characterization of the distinguished unipotent orbits of a connected reductive group over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0. For classical groups we prove the characterization by a combinatorial computation, and for exceptional groups we check it with a computer. This characterization is needed in the theory of cuspidal sheaves on the stack of L-parameters in the article ``Cuspidal sheaves on the stack of L-parameters'' of the first two authors.

papers.title: The Gromov-Lawson-Rosenberg Conjecture for Z/4xZ/4
papers.abstract: We prove the Gromov-Lawson-Rosenberg Conjecture for the group Z/4xZ/4 by computing the connective real k-homology of the classifying space with the Adams spectral sequence and two types of detection theorems for the kernel of the alpha invariant: one based on eta-invariants, closely following work of Botvinnik-Gilkey-Stolz, and a second one based on homological methods. Along the way, we determine differentials of the Adams spectral sequence for classifying spaces involved in the computation, and we study the cap structure of the Adams spectral sequence for sub-hopf algebras of the Steenrod algebra relevant to the computation of connective real and complex k-homology.

papers.title: Musielak-Orlicz-Sobolev embeddings: Necessary and Sufficient Conditions
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the necessary and sufficient conditions on domain for Musielak-Orlicz-Sobolev embedding of the space $W^{1,Φ(\cdot,\cdot)}(Ω)$ where $Φ(x,t):=t^{p(x)}{(\log(e+t))}^{q(x)}.$

papers.title: On the modelling and prediction of high-dimensional functional time series
papers.abstract: We propose a two-step procedure to model and predict high-dimensional functional time series, where the number of function-valued time series $p$ is large in relation to the length of time series $n$. Our first step performs an eigenanalysis of a positive definite matrix, which leads to a one-to-one linear transformation for the original high-dimensional functional time series, and the transformed curve series can be segmented into several groups such that any two subseries from any two different groups are uncorrelated both contemporaneously and serially. Consequently in our second step those groups are handled separately without the information loss on the overall linear dynamic structure. The second step is devoted to establishing a finite-dimensional dynamical structure for all the transformed functional time series within each group. Furthermore the finite-dimensional structure is represented by that of a vector time series. Modelling and forecasting for the original high-dimensional functional time series are realized via those for the vector time series in all the groups. We investigate the theoretical properties of our proposed methods, and illustrate the finite-sample performance through both extensive simulation and two real datasets.

papers.title: Families of two dimensional modular $(\varphi,Γ)$-modules
papers.abstract: Let $F/{\mathbb Q}_p$ be a finite unramified extension, let $k$ be a finite extension of the residue field of $F$. We provide explicit constructions of integral structures for all rank two étale Lubin-Tate $(\varphi,{\mathcal O}_F^{\times})$-modules over $k$. We construct algebraic families of such integral structures and show that these comprehensively reflect the degeneration behaviour of $(\varphi,{\mathcal O}_F^{\times})$-modules. These results reveal new combinatorial structures of the moduli stack of $(\varphi,{\mathcal O}_F^{\times})$-modules, and allow us, in particular, to rederive the fact that the Serre weights assigned to a two dimensional ${\rm Gal}(\overline{F}/F)$-representation over $k$ can be read off from the geometry of the stack.

papers.title: A Unified Algorithmic Framework for Dynamic Assortment Optimization under MNL Choice
papers.abstract: We consider assortment and inventory planning problems with dynamic stockout-based substitution effects, and without replenishment, in two different settings: (1) Customers can see all available products when they arrive, a typical scenario in physical stores. (2) The seller can choose to offer a subset of available products to each customer, which is more common on online platforms. Both settings are known to be computationally challenging, and the current approximation algorithms for the two settings are quite different. We develop a unified algorithm framework under the MNL choice model for both settings. Our algorithms improve on the state-of-the-art algorithms in terms of approximation guarantee and runtime, and the ability to manage uncertainty in the total number of customers and handle more complex constraints. In the process, we establish various novel properties of dynamic assortment planning (for the MNL choice model) that may be useful more broadly.

papers.title: FedADMM-InSa: An Inexact and Self-Adaptive ADMM for Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is a promising framework for learning from distributed data while maintaining privacy. The development of efficient FL algorithms encounters various challenges, including heterogeneous data and systems, limited communication capacities, and constrained local computational resources. Recently developed FedADMM methods show great resilience to both data and system heterogeneity. However, they still suffer from performance deterioration if the hyperparameters are not carefully tuned. To address this issue, we propose an inexact and self-adaptive FedADMM algorithm, termed FedADMM-InSa. First, we design an inexactness criterion for the clients' local updates to eliminate the need for empirically setting the local training accuracy. This inexactness criterion can be assessed by each client independently based on its unique condition, thereby reducing the local computational cost and mitigating the undesirable straggle effect. The convergence of the resulting inexact ADMM is proved under the assumption of strongly convex loss functions. Additionally, we present a self-adaptive scheme that dynamically adjusts each client's penalty parameter, enhancing algorithm robustness by mitigating the need for empirical penalty parameter choices for each client. Extensive numerical experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets are conducted. As validated by some numerical tests, our proposed algorithm can reduce the clients' local computational load significantly and also accelerate the learning process compared to the vanilla FedADMM. The source code is available at https://github.com/DCN-FAU-AvH/FedADMM-InSa.

papers.title: Stein Boltzmann Sampling: A Variational Approach for Global Optimization
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present a flow-based method for global optimization of continuous Sobolev functions, called Stein Boltzmann Sampling (SBS). SBS initializes uniformly a number of particles representing candidate solutions, then uses the Stein Variational Gradient Descent (SVGD) algorithm to sequentially and deterministically move those particles in order to approximate a target distribution whose mass is concentrated around promising areas of the domain of the optimized function. The target is chosen to be a properly parametrized Boltzmann distribution. For the purpose of global optimization, we adapt the generic SVGD theoretical framework allowing to address more general target distributions over a compact subset of $\mathbb{R}^d$, and we prove SBS's asymptotic convergence. In addition to the main SBS algorithm, we present two variants: the SBS-PF that includes a particle filtering strategy, and the SBS-HYBRID one that uses SBS or SBS-PF as a continuation after other particle- or distribution-based optimization methods. A detailed comparison with state-of-the-art methods on benchmark functions demonstrates that SBS and its variants are highly competitive, while the combination of the two variants provides the best trade-off between accuracy and computational cost.

papers.title: Heat kernel estimates for boundary traces of reflected diffusions on uniform domains
papers.abstract: We study the boundary trace processes of reflected diffusions on uniform domains. We obtain stable-like heat kernel estimates for such a boundary trace process when the diffusion on the underlying ambient space satisfies sub-Gaussian heat kernel estimates. Our arguments rely on new results of independent interest such as sharp two-sided estimates and the volume doubling property of the harmonic measure, the existence of a continuous extension of the Naïm kernel to the topological boundary, and the Doob--Naïm formula identifying the Dirichlet form of the boundary trace process as the pure-jump Dirichlet form whose jump kernel with respect to the harmonic measure is exactly (the continuous extension of) the Naïm kernel.

papers.title: A sharper bound of the Hotelling-Solomons inequality
papers.abstract: The original Hotelling-Solomons inequality states that an upper bound of the absolute difference between the mean and median, standardized by the standard deviation, is 1. However, in this paper, we introduce a new bound that depends on the sample size, which is strictly smaller than 1.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning for optimal dividend problem under diffusion model
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the optimal dividend problem under the continuous time diffusion model with the bounded dividend rate from the Reinforcement Learning (RL) perspective. Unlike the standard literature, our main focus will be on numerical algorithms that allow part or all of the system parameters to be unspecified so that the optimal control cannot be explicitly determined. Following the RL literature we introduce the entropy-regularized exploratory control problem, which randomizes the control actions and balances the levels of exploitation and exploration, and carry out a theoretical analysis of the associated Policy Improvement (PI) and Policy Evaluation (PE) devices and the corresponding sequence of the approximating optimal strategies. Specifically, our algorithm will be based on two independent neural networks that approximate the value function and its derivative simultaneously. Such an algorithm, to the best of our knowledge, is new in the context of the optimal dividend problems, and can be effective even for the situation when the premium and/or interest rate is state dependent, hence beyond reach of the standard statistical methods. Some numerical experiments are presented to empirically demonstrate the effectiveness of our RL algorithm.

papers.title: Approximate and Weighted Data Reconstruction Attack in Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a distributed learning paradigm that enables multiple clients to collaborate on building a machine learning model without sharing their private data. Although FL is considered privacy-preserved by design, recent data reconstruction attacks demonstrate that an attacker can recover clients' training data based on the parameters shared in FL. However, most existing methods fail to attack the most widely used horizontal Federated Averaging (FedAvg) scenario, where clients share model parameters after multiple local training steps. To tackle this issue, we propose an interpolation-based approximation method, which makes attacking FedAvg scenarios feasible by generating the intermediate model updates of the clients' local training processes. Then, we design a layer-wise weighted loss function to improve the data quality of reconstruction. We assign different weights to model updates in different layers concerning the neural network structure, with the weights tuned by Bayesian optimization. Finally, experimental results validate the superiority of our proposed approximate and weighted attack (AWA) method over the other state-of-the-art methods, as demonstrated by the substantial improvement in different evaluation metrics for image data reconstructions. The source code is available at https://github.com/DCN-FAU-AvH/FL-AWA-attack.

papers.title: Macroscopic diffusive fluctuations for generalized hard rods dynamics
papers.abstract: We study the fluctuations in equilibrium for a dynamics of rods with random length. This includes the classical hard rod elastic collisions, when rod lengths are constant and equal to a positive value. We prove that in the diffusive space-time scaling, an initial fluctuation of density of particles of velocity $v$, after recentering on its Euler evolution, evolve randomly shifted by a Brownian motion of variance $\mathcal D(v)$.

papers.title: Parabolic stochastic quantisation of the fractional $Φ^4_3$ model in the full subcritical regime
papers.abstract: We present a construction of the measure of the fractional $Φ^4$ Euclidean quantum field theory on $\mathbb{R}^3$ in the full subcritical regime via parabolic stochastic quantisation. Our approach is based on a truncated flow equation for the effective description of the model at sufficiently small scales and on coercive estimates for the nonlinear stochastic partial differential equation describing the interacting field. The constructed measure is translation invariant, reflection positive, and has quartic exponential tails.

papers.title: Testing the equality of the copulas of two multivariate populations with Bernstein polynomials
papers.abstract: The empirical Bernstein copula process is utilized to conduct tests for the equal- ity of the dependence structures between two samples. To this end, three tests statistics are proposed, and their asymptotic properties are established under mild regularity conditions. Furthermore, in order to obtain a valid p-value, sub- sampling and multiplier bootstrap methods are introduced and investigated for the Bernstein based-test statistics. Through a simulation study, it is shown that Bernstein-based tests significantly outperform tests based on the empirical copula.

papers.title: A Simple Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis
papers.abstract: In this article, it is proved that the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function must lie on the critical line, known as the Riemann hypothesis.

papers.title: On properties of the generalized Davenport Expansion
papers.abstract: We study the continuity properties of a generalized Davenport Fourier expansion we recently discovered, by imposing conditions on the coefficients. We also put our expansion into perspective from the position of Appell sequences.

papers.title: Triangular prism equations and categorification
papers.abstract: We obtain the triangular prism equations by evaluating a labelled prism in two ways, as a sum of products of two or of three tetrahedral coefficients. For a spherical fusion category an explicit change of variables identifies these equations with the pentagon equations. Prisms with repeated edge labels yield local subsystems, simplified using tetrahedral rotations and the Fuchs-Runkel-Schweigert parity theorem. Additional prism equations couple these subsystems. Two further obstructions, the zero- and one-spectrum criteria, follow directly from the pentagon equations and apply over every field without a pivotal structure. We prove that F210 admits no fusion categorification in characteristic zero and no pivotal fusion categorification in positive characteristic, and that F660 admits no fusion categorification over any field. Together with a bounded census and known unitary obstructions, these results classify, up to Grothendieck equivalence, the non-pointed unitary simple integral fusion categories of rank at most 8 and Frobenius-Perron dimension at most 20000 for which the Frobenius-Perron dimension of each simple object divides that of the category.

papers.title: Resolvent convergence under heterogeneous second-moment profiles and quadratic-form control
papers.abstract: Let $X=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}$ have independent real columns with finite second moments, not necessarily centered or identically distributed. For $z\in\mathbb C\setminus[0,\infty)$, we compare \[ G^z=\left(\frac1nXX^\top-zI_p\right)^{-1} \] with a deterministic matrix $\tilde G^z$ defined by the second-moment profile $(Σ_i)_{i\in[n]}$, where $Σ_i=\mathbb E[x_ix_i^\top]$. For deterministic matrices \(A\), we prove finite-dimensional \(L^q\) bounds for $\tr(A(G^z-\tilde G^z))$ in terms of moments of centered quadratic forms, without assuming independence among the coordinates of a column. Operator-test bounds impose no trace-growth or aspect-ratio restriction and display explicitly the effect of the sizes and repetitions of the second-moment matrices $(Σ_i)_{i\in[n]}$. Under $\sqrt p\sup_{i\in[n]}|Σ_i|_{\hs}=O(n)$, the Hilbert-Schmidt bounds involve approximation of the profile by commuting positive-semidefinite matrices, with explicit dependence on the approximation error and the dimension of their span. We also obtain corresponding bounds for \(\tr(A G^z B G^z)\), with deterministic \(A,B\). All bounds are locally uniform in $z\in\mathbb C\setminus[0,\infty)$.

papers.title: Classification of the d-representation-finite symmetric k-algebras of finite representation type
papers.abstract: We give a complete classification of all $d$-representation-finite symmetric Nakayama algebras and of all $d$-representation-finite trivial extensions of path algebras of quivers, over an arbitrary field. As a consequence we get a classification, up to Morita equivalence, of all $d$-representation-finite symmetric algebras of finite representation type over an algebraically closed field.

papers.title: Forcing the $Π^1_n$-Uniformization Property
papers.abstract: We generically construct a model in which the ${Π^1_3}$-uniformization property is true, thus lowering the best known consistency strength from the existence of $M_1^{\#}$ to just $\mathsf{ZFC}$. The forcing construction can be adapted to work over canonical inner models with Woodin cardinals, which yields, for the first time, universes where the $Π^1_{2n}$-uniformization property holds for $n >1$, thus producing models which contradict the natural $\mathsf{PD}$-induced pattern.

papers.title: Convergence in Wasserstein Distance for Empirical Measures of Semilinear SPDEs
papers.abstract: The convergence rate in Wasserstein distance is estimated for the empirical measures of symmetric semilinear SPDEs. Unlike in the finite-dimensional case that the convergence is of algebraic order in time, in the present situation the convergence is of log order with a power given by eigenvalues of the underlying linear operator.

papers.title: A Divisor Function Inequality
papers.abstract: This short note provides a sharper upper bound of a well known inequality for the sum of divisors function. This is a problem in pure mathematics related to the distribution of prime numbers. Furthermore, the technique is completely elementary.

papers.title: On Fourier frames
papers.abstract: We solve the problem of Duffin and Schaeffer (1952) of characterizing those sequences of real frequencies which generate Fourier frames. Equivalently, we characterize the sampling sequences for the Paley-Wiener space. The key step is to connect the problem with de Branges' theory of Hilbert spaces of entire functions. We show that our description of sampling sequences permits us to obtain a classical inequality of H. Landau as a consequence of Pavlov's description of Riesz bases of complex exponentials and the John-Nirenberg theorem. Finally, we discuss how to transform our description into a working condition by relating it to an approximation problem for subharmonic functions. By this approach, we determine the critical growth rate of a nondecreasing function $ψ$ such that the sequence $\{\lamdda_k\}){k\in \Bbb Z}$ defined by $λ_k + ψ(λ_k)=k$ is a sampling.

papers.title: TSP instances that require exponentially many subtour elimination constraints
papers.abstract: We construct pathological TSP instances that require exponentially many subtour elimination constraints (SECs) in the sense that, if a smaller collection of SECs is imposed, then the Dantzig-Fulkerson-Johnson model returns a disconnected solution costing less than an optimal tour. For asymmetric instances on $n$ vertices, we prove a growth rate of \(Ω(φ^n)\), where \(φ\approx 1.618\) is the golden ratio. A node-splitting reduction gives metric instances with \(Ω(φ^{n/2})\) growth. We also give instances in the plane under the Euclidean, Rectilinear, and Maximum metrics that require exponentially many SECs. Concorde struggles on them, with solve times growing exponentially despite tiny integrality gaps.

papers.title: Erratum to Power boundedness and related properties for weighted composition operators on $\mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$, Journal of Functional Analysis 288 (2025), 110745
papers.abstract: As was kindly pointed out to us by S. Li, the proofs of Theorem 2.11 and Lemma 3.1 in our original paper contain errors that require modifications of the corresponding statements. We also correct a gap in the proof of Lemma 2.1, whose statement remains valid. Furthermore, we explain the consequences for several subsequent results and provide the necessary corrections to their statements and proofs.

papers.title: Toward a Holographic Representation Theory of the Bosonic de Sitter Discrete Series
papers.abstract: We propose a program toward a holographic representation theory of the non-scalar bosonic discrete series $Π^\pm_{p,q}$, $p,q\in\mathbb{N}$, $1\leqslant q\leqslant p$, of the de Sitter ($\mathrm{dS}_{4}$) group $G=\mathrm{SO}_0(1,4)$. The proposal exploits two complementary realizations of the same unitary irreducible representation (UIR): a bounded-domain realization on an open ball $\mathbb{B}$ modeling the hyperbolic space $G/\mathrm{SO}(4)$, with $\partial\mathbb{B}\simeq\mathbb{S}^{3}$, and a covariant spacetime realization on $\mathrm{dS}_{4}$, with conformal boundaries $\mathscr{I}^{\pm}\simeq\mathbb{S}^{3}$, in which the physical UIR is obtained through the corresponding gauge reduction. This leads to two boundary constructions and an explicit compatibility problem, \begin{align*} \mathbb{B} \;\overset{?\mathrm{hol}}{\longleftrightarrow}\; \partial\mathbb{B}\simeq\mathbb{S}^{3} \quad\overset{?}{\simeq}\quad \mathscr{I}^{\pm}\simeq\mathbb{S}^{3} \;\overset{?\mathrm{hol}}{\longleftrightarrow}\; \mathrm{dS}_{4} \,. \end{align*} The two outer problems seek explicit intertwiners between the bulk and boundary realizations, with their invariant norms, constraints, and physical quotients properly identified. The middle problem asks how to construct and normalize a unitary intertwiner between the two boundary realizations once both have been shown to carry the same UIR. The bounded picture exposes the unitary and harmonic structure of the representation, while the spacetime picture makes its covariant and gauge-theoretic structure manifest, allowing the two constructions to constrain and illuminate one another. The established scalar family $Π_{p,0}$, $p\in\mathbb{N}$, with its spherical realization on $\mathbb{S}^{3}$, provides the guiding prototype. Particular attention is given to ...

papers.title: Region Coloring of Spatial Graphs using Knot-theoretic Ternary Quasigroups
papers.abstract: We construct coloring conditions around vertices for region colorings of unoriented spatial graph diagrams by knot-theoretic ternary quasigroups. These conditions require cyclic products of left and right operators around each vertex to be the identity. We prove that the resulting coloring sets are preserved under the generalized Reidemeister moves and relate our construction to the palette framework. We show that the vertex coloring conditions are automatic for Dehn tribrackets and determine the associated palettes for unoriented Alexander tribrackets. We also introduce an additional restriction on vertex colorings that is preserved under the fifth Reidemeister move for every unoriented knot-theoretic ternary quasigroup. This restriction gives rise to further coloring invariants for Dehn tribrackets and unoriented Alexander tribrackets.

papers.title: A $19/5$ lower bound for the four-dimensional Erdős box problem
papers.abstract: For every power $q\ge2$ of~$2$, we construct a box-free subset of $[q^5]^4$ with $q^{19}$ points, improving the lower-bound exponent in the four-dimensional Erdős box problem from $15/4$ to $19/5$. In fact, $[q^5]^4$ partitions into $q$ isomorphic box-free sets. The proof uses a finite-field rectangle lemma and orthogonality in a four-dimensional bilinear space. We also deduce a uniform bound $f_4(n)\ge2^{-19/20}n^{19/5}$ and a lower bound for grid-coloring numbers.

papers.title: Evolution of Internal Waves on Surfaces of Revolution with Flat Ends
papers.abstract: We generalize the 2D linear internal wave equation to non-compact surfaces of revolution with flat ends. We show that the leading profile of this equation with oscillatory forcing is the unique incoming solution to the corresponding stationary equation. This is done by proving a limiting absorption principle via propagation of semiclassical defect measure.

papers.title: Subgroup distortion in free-by-cyclic groups with linearly growing monodromy
papers.abstract: Let $G=F\rtimes_φ\mathbb Z$ be the mapping torus of a linearly growing UPG automorphism $φ$ of a finitely generated free group $F$. We compute the distortion of every finitely generated subgroup $H$ of $G$, and we show that it is linear, quadratic or exponential. In contrast, for each $d\ge2$, Dison and Riley constructed an automorphism of polynomial degree $d$ whose mapping torus contains a free subgroup with distortion equivalent to the Ackermann function $A_{d+1}$, which grows faster than every iterated exponential function. Using the natural splitting of $G$ over $\mathbb Z^2$ subgroups and its topological representative, we associate to $H$ a family of \emph{horizontal components}, together with \emph{dilation homomorphisms} defined from slopes along these components. We prove that $H$ is undistorted in $G$ if and only if every horizontal component of $H$ consists of only one piece. Otherwise, the distortion of $H$ is quadratic if all dilation homomorphisms are trivial, and exponential if one of them is nontrivial. Along the way, we show that the distortion of $H$ is determined, up to superadditive closure, by the distortions of the stabilizers of its horizontal components.

papers.title: Baxter $\mathbb{Q}$-operator and Separation of Variables for BC-type open $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ spin chain
papers.abstract: We construct two-parameter Baxter $\mathbb{Q}$-operators for the transfer matrices of noncompact open $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ BC-type spin chains with general boundary interactions, treating both one-boundary and two-boundary models. The $\mathbb{Q}$-operators are defined as traces of general monodromy matrices over infinite-dimensional auxiliary spaces carrying principal series representations of $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$. At specific values of parameters the two-parameter $\mathbb{Q}$-operators degenerate into simpler one-parameter Baxter operators. We prove that the general transfer matrices factorize into products of these one-parameter $Q$-operators. We provide both an algebraic derivation based on local operator identities and a diagrammatic proof using Feynman diagrammatic techniques. Finally, we apply the quantum Separation of Variables (SoV) method to the spectral problem of the one-boundary transfer matrix. We derive the system of separated difference equations for the transfer matrix eigenfunctions and show that, under the assumption of kernel factorization, it reduces to a one-dimensional difference equation coinciding precisely with the Baxter equation for eigenvalues of appropriately normalized one-parameter Baxter $Q$-operator.

papers.title: Addendum to "Geodesic fields for Pontryagin type $C^0$-Finsler manifolds"
papers.abstract: In the paper ``Geodesic fields for Pontryagin type $C^0$-Finsler manifolds'', the same authors introduced a geometric object called Pontryagin-type $C^0$-Finsler structures, which includes Finsler structures on a smooth manifold $M$. Such a structure is defined locally by a control system of $C^1$ unit vector fields on an open subset $U$ of $M$, such that Pontryagin's maximum principle (PMP) is applicable. As a result of PMP, we obtain the extended geodesic field $\mathcal{E}$, which is a multivalued vector field on the slit cotangent bundle $T^{\ast}U\backslash 0 = \{(x,α): x\in U, α\in T^{\ast}_x U\}$, such that every minimizing path $x(t)$ on $(U,F)$ is an extremal (projection of a Pontryagin extremal $(x(t),α(t))$). Some time after its introduction, its use and external comments, it is useful to provide remarks that clarify the applicability and limitations of this theory. In addition, we point out two errors contained in that work which, although discernible from the context, we believe should be pointed out. Finally, we prove some cases where the property that a minimizing path is the projection of a Pontryagin extremal can be extended beyond a coordinate system, sometimes to $M$. We also work on the problem of determining when $\mathcal{E}$ does not depend on the control system chosen to represent $F$. In particular, $\mathcal{E}$ satisfies these two properties globally for left-invariant $C^0$-Finsler structures on Lie groups, and for $C^1$-Finsler structures (without the condition of strong convexity).

papers.title: Convergence rates for truncated and discretised signature expansions
papers.abstract: Linear expansions in Brownian Stratonovich signatures, which originate in stochastic Taylor expansions, are increasingly used to represent and model processes with memory. Their numerical use requires truncating the signature at a level $M$ and discretising the driving path along $N$ steps. Under a simple growth condition on the coefficients of the linear expansion, we establish strong and weak convergence rates for both approximations, uniformly in time. The strong truncation error decays like $(B^M/(M!)^\varepsilon)^a$ for some constant $B$, uniformly in $N$, where $\varepsilon$ measures the growth of the coefficients and $a$ the regularity of the test function; the weak error does not improve on it. The discretisation error is of order $N^{-a/2}$ in $L^p$, and $N^{-1}$ weakly for polynomial test functions, uniformly in $M$. All these rates are sharp for polynomial test functions, and $M$, $N$ can be chosen independently. We extend the estimates to errors in probability, on distribution functions and on risk measures, and illustrate them on stochastic delay equations, Volterra processes and option pricing in signature volatility models.

papers.title: Minimal Finite Non-Commutative Centrally Essential Rings
papers.abstract: A ring $R$ with nonzero unity is called centrally essential if for every nonzero element $a$ of $R$ there exist nonzero central elements $x$ and $y$ such that $ax = y$. In this paper we obtain a complete classification, up to isomorphism, of non-commutative centrally essential rings of minimal order $64$.

papers.title: An Optimized Expansion Auction Integrating Energy, Flexibility, and Network Constraints
papers.abstract: Auction mechanisms are widely used to support generation investments. In the US, capacity auctions serve as supply-adequacy instruments to address the missing-money problem, whereas in Latin America, energy and capacity auctions procure long-term contracts to support generation expansion. In both settings, accreditation metrics, such as Firm Energy (FE) and Effective Load Carrying Capability (ELCC), are used to approximate the reliability contribution of selected units and winning projects are selected based on a financial offer. This approach fails to recognize the actual contribution of winners to the multiple services they provide to the system. This limitation becomes more significant with high shares of renewables, as the value of each resource increasingly depends on network and technological constraints, as well as on complementarities within the generation portfolio. Inspired by short-term auctions, such as day-ahead markets, this paper proposes a joint optimization-based auction for generation and transmission investments that internalizes these interactions, capturing the intrinsic value of generation candidates without requiring the computation of FE or ELCC metrics. The auctioneer determines the winning portfolio through an expansion-planning model that explicitly represents network constraints, operational interactions, reliability standards, and multiple scenarios. A case study of the Brazilian system indicates lower system costs, lower risk, and a more diverse portfolio relative to the stylized decoupled procurement approaches currently deployed in many systems.

papers.title: Every classifiable stably finite $C^*$-algebra has an untwisted étale groupoid model
papers.abstract: We show that every classifiable stably finite $C^*$-algebra is isomorphic to the $C^*$-algebra of a second countable, locally compact Hausdorff, principal étale groupoid. Equivalently, every such $C^*$-algebra has a $C^*$-diagonal whose Weyl twist is trivial. Together with Evington and Sibbel's recent result for all UCT Kirchberg algebras, this provides untwisted principal groupoid models for every classifiable $C^*$-algebra.

papers.title: Simple Length Multiplicity on X(n)
papers.abstract: We study multiplicity among lengths of simple closed geodesics on the principal congruence surfaces $X(n)=Γ(n)\backslash\mathbb{H}$. We show that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there are positive constants $n_\varepsilon,C_{\varepsilon}$ so that, for $n\ge n_\varepsilon$, there are at least $\exp((\frac{π^2}{12}-\varepsilon)n)$ simple closed geodesics on $X(n)$ of the same length $\ell<C_\varepsilon n$. We produce the same multiplicity for $λ$-length of simple arcs with distinct endpoints via the McShane identity, which is immediately relevant as the size of a McShane gap around such an arc is roughly the reciprocal square of its $λ$-length. Our method of proof relies on an independently interesting theorem about the McShane identity for $X(n)$: the total mass of the gaps of pants with two cusps tends to 1 as $n\to \infty$. We present a proof of this latter fact that relies on estimates for the speed of mixing provided by Selberg's 3/16-Theorem (discovered with the help of ChatGPT). We indicate several avenues for further investigation.

papers.title: On the atomic decomposition of complete intersections in toric varieties
papers.abstract: Building on Liu's and Liu--Sheshmani's systematized description of Kontsevich's localization methods in toric varieties, we develop a computational framework for genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants of smooth projective toric varieties and their smooth complete intersections. This is grounded in equivariant localization and the combinatorial structure of toric fans. We describe how the geometric data required by the localization formulas can be recovered directly from the fan and extend the existing software for flag varieties to compute the small quantum multiplication by the first Chern class. The implementation also incorporates cyclic determinants and regularized-exponent multisets, providing computational tools for investigating the atomic decomposition of quantum cohomology. Using this framework, we obtain the nonrationality of every smooth complete intersection of a quadric and a cubic in $\mathbb{P}^5$. Also applying new methods to study Hodge atoms in Fano fivefolds, we recover the nonrationality of every smooth complete intersection of a quadric and a cubic in $\mathbb{P}^7$, due to Cavenaghi--Katzarkov--Kontsevich, and we prove the nonrationality of every smooth quartic double fivefold and every smooth quartic fivefold.

papers.title: Rigid Theories
papers.abstract: A structure is rigid if it admits no non-trivial automorphisms. We investigate an analogous invariance property for first-order theories, with relative interpretations playing the role of morphisms. A theory $T$ is called rigid if and only if every self-interpretation of $T$ is definably isomorphic to the identity interpretation. Extending work of Pakhomov and Zapryagaev (2020) on Presburger Arithmetic, we establish rigidity for Successor Arithmetic and Skolem Arithmetic (with respect to one-dimensional interpretations), True Arithmetic, and the theories of fields $\mathrm{RCF}$ and $\mathrm{ACF}$. By contrast, $\mathrm{PA}$ and $\mathrm{ZF}$ admit infinitely many self-interpretations, though both remain rigid with respect to (co-)retractions. Our main negative result is that $\mathrm{ZFC}$ has no consistent rigid extension in its own language. We compare rigidity with categoricity, model rigidity, completeness, and solidity, showing it to be independent of the first three, and indicate the relevance of rigidity to questions about semantic determinacy.

papers.title: Prime values of linear forms and a quadratic form: one proof and two arithmetic applications
